introduced.quote: It is apparent that the pages have been referenced often, and that this was the personal notebook of Artistic Director Aurelie.

introduced.name: Vacher
introduced.how: the captor behind the serial kidnappings and murders
introduced.quote: proving Vacher's guilt

introduced.name: Sedene
introduced.how: Palais Mermonia staff who handles requests to review recovered evidence
introduced.quote: ...you want to review some recovered items connected to victims of the serial disappearances case?

introduced.name: Palais Mermonia
introduced.how: a site where recovered evidence from the disappearances case is kept
introduced.quote: Come, let's pay a visit to the Palais Mermonia.

introduced.name: Opera Epiclese
introduced.how: the grandest stage in Fontaine, which must be booked for events
introduced.quote: By which I of course mean, the Opera Epiclese.

introduced.name: Neuvillette
introduced.how: the person whose go-ahead and staff control booking the Opera Epiclese
introduced.quote: We'll need to get the go-ahead from Neuvillette — I know just where to find him.

introduced.name: Clio
introduced.how: the protagonist of The Little Oceanid, whose choices are modeled on Furina's own
introduced.quote: The experiences and decisions of the protagonist, Clio, are all modeled after your own.

introduced.name: The Little Oceanid
introduced.how: a musical the troupe is staging, about a mermaid who gives up her voice to become human
introduced.quote: "The Little Oceanid" cannot be complete unless we do justice to Aurelie on an emotional level.

introduced.name: Aurelie's Notes
introduced.how: Aurelie's diary written during her captivity, with lyrics on later pages
introduced.quote: So this is all Aurelie left behind... Just whatever she was carrying on her person, and this tattered old notebook.

introduced.name: Aurelie's kidnapping and murder
introduced.how: Aurelie was kidnapped and killed by Sinthe dealers after Vilmant's sponsorship deal went wrong
introduced.quote: You brought the director to the attention of the Sinthe dealers.

introduced.name: Sinthe sponsorship deal
introduced.how: Vilmant accepted a merchant's sponsorship without consulting the director, which led to the Sinthe dealers' pressure
introduced.quote: So anyway, one day after a show, a merchant came to me and offered us a huge sponsorship.

introduced.name: Dissolving experiments
introduced.how: captives were dissolved in experiments carried out by the captor
introduced.quote: She watched a girl get dissolved right in front of her...

assumed.name: Furina
assumed.quote: She's still an idol to many people in Fontaine, including myself...

assumed.name: Katheryne
assumed.quote: Eh, Paimon's just being enthusiastic. We're old friends now, she gets it!

assumed.name: Palais Mermonia
assumed.quote: She used to live in luxury at the Palais Mermonia, but she's, uh... moved out, right?

assumed.name: Vision
assumed.quote: I don't even have a Vision, you know.

assumed.name: Gardemek
assumed.quote: We looked for her, the Gardemeks looked for her, but she was nowhere to be found.

assumed.name: Sedene
assumed.quote: As the Traveler had been an investigator on the case, Sedene goes to look for the items and shortly returns with a diary and other belongings she had on her person.

assumed.name: Neuvillette
assumed.quote: so she and the Traveler go off to find Neuvillette, who Furina predicts will be taking a break outside the Palais Mermonia.

assumed.name: Hydro Archon
assumed.quote: And I'm not even the Hydro Archon anymore, so all my power is gone anyway.

assumed.name: Serial disappearances case
assumed.quote: Isn't that the drink peddled by the culprit behind the serial disappearances case?

assumed.name: Underwater Sinthe base
assumed.quote: You once investigated that underwater Sinthe base, and recovered items belonging to the victims.

assumed.name: The Steambird
assumed.quote: You'll probably be able to read all about it in the Steambird first thing tomorrow morning.

assumed.name: The troupe
assumed.quote: As you all know already, the troupe was kept afloat not from ticket sales, but donations from the audience.

assumed.name: Dulphy's illness
assumed.quote: Dulphy, are you sure you can manage in your condition?

assumed.name: Vision
assumed.quote: was about to drop the prop Vision

threads.claim: Aurelie's disappearance appears to be tied to the serial disappearances case, though the details remain unclear.
threads.quote: Increasingly, all the signs seemed to point to her being the latest victim in the serial disappearances case.

threads.claim: The true culprit of the serial disappearances was brought to justice thanks to the Traveler and Paimon.
threads.quote: That's actually how I recognized these two. It was all thanks to their efforts that the true culprit was brought to justice.

threads.claim: Aurelie told the troupe to leave the city and wait for her outside, then vanished without a trace.
threads.quote: On the day when she went missing, Director Aurelie had instructed us all — somewhat out the blue — to leave the Court of Fontaine and wait for her outside the city.

threads.claim: Aurelie may have known in advance what was about to happen and was moving the troupe to safety.
threads.quote: Hmm... But doesn't the way she suddenly told you to leave the city suggest that maybe she had some sense of what was about to happen?

threads.claim: Vilmant seems to know something about Aurelie's fate but refuses to open up to Pauleau.
threads.quote: Vilmant might know something, but he won't open up to me.

threads.claim: The water in the land may be a conscious entity that fled because of human pollution.
threads.quote: In the end, they discover that all the waste and pollution created by humans over the years has caused the fresh water to flee the land, as if driven by a consciousness of its own.

threads.claim: Furina's freedom from the Hydro Archon role brings loneliness, since she feels she is no longer needed.
threads.quote: But on some level, freedom also means no longer being needed. I have no further use to people.

threads.claim: Furina has a secret she swore to protect and has never been able to share it with anyone.
threads.quote: I was scared of someone recognizing me for who I truly was, and exposing the secret I swore to protect.

threads.claim: Furina has decided to retire from the stage and refuses to play any new roles.
threads.quote: True, but I have made a decision to retire from the stage.

threads.claim: Some people in Poisson still resent the Hydro Archon for failing to prevent the catastrophe.
threads.quote: not everyone here is ready to forgive and forget after the Hydro Archon's inaction in the face of catastrophe.

threads.claim: Furina receives a Vision of her own, which she uses in place of the gem on her waist.
threads.quote: Furina is also left surprised at receiving a Vision, already using it in place of the large gem on her waist.

threads.claim: Dulphy's chronic illness flares up again and forces Furina to take over her role.
threads.quote: Dulphy's illness returns and incapacitates her, forcing Furina to assume her role for the final scene

threads.claim: Pauleau was in love with Aurelie, who had rejected him and whom he now cannot pursue.
threads.quote: I was deeply, madly in love with Aurelie.

threads.claim: The troupe has not decided whether the musical's ending should be happy or a true-to-life tragedy.
threads.quote: We still haven't decided between a happy ending or a true-to-life tragedy.

threads.claim: Furina hopes the people of Poisson can forgive her for her failure, but expects their resentment.
threads.quote: I'd be overjoyed if the people here could find it in their hearts to forgive me.

threads.claim: Aurelie's fate is an open question that the Traveler suggests may be discoverable.
threads.quote: It might actually be possible to find out more about her fate.

threads.claim: Aurelie's notebook reveals her captor's actions and the conditions of her final days.
threads.quote: Looks like she kept a detailed record of her captor's actions.

threads.claim: Aurelie's notes echo the mermaid's bargain about giving up a secret and facing suffering.
threads.quote: You can reveal your secret to no one. You will face suffering and loneliness.

threads.claim: Aurelie did not regret her final choice even as she waited for death.
threads.quote: So she didn't regret her decision. Even as she sat in silence, waiting for death to come.

threads.claim: The Sinthe dealers keep pressuring the troupe, escalating the threat to Aurelie.
threads.quote: The Sinthe merchant just wouldn't let up.

threads.claim: Aurelie's notebook would have served as conclusive evidence against Vacher.
threads.quote: proving Vacher's guilt

threads.claim: Dulphy has a serious condition that the group is worried about.
threads.quote: Dulphy, are you sure you can manage in your condition?

threads.claim: Dulphy's medication has been losing effectiveness, so she has been raising her dose.
threads.quote: They've... been getting less and less effective over time.

threads.claim: Neuvillette suggests Furina's own experiences mirror those of Clio.
threads.quote: The experiences and decisions of the protagonist, Clio, are all modeled after your own.

threads.claim: Furina feels she has regained freedom and curiosity after giving up her divine status.
threads.quote: Maybe it's because I've finally become an ordinary person, and gained my freedom, that I've developed a great sense of curiosity about their lives.

threads.claim: Furina is reconsidering a return to the stage despite having sworn off acting.
threads.quote: I still don't wish to pretend to be someone else, but I do have a desire to express myself...

threads.claim: A real Vision appeared out of thin air during the show, and no one knows why.
threads.quote: I've got no idea what happened there, either.

threads.claim: Furina treats the Vision as a gift from the gods that she intends to honor.
threads.quote: If a Vision is a gift from the gods...

introduced.name: Emilie
introduced.how: a famous perfumer and flower expert who has helped Chevreuse solve difficult cases before
introduced.quote: She's a good friend of mine. She's lent me her aid several times in the past to resolve some difficult cases.

introduced.name: Rainbow Rose
introduced.how: the killer's rose came from a very rare cultivar, traced to a single place in Fontaine
introduced.quote: But according to Emilie, the Rainbow Rose left by the killer was derived from a very rare cultivar.

introduced.name: Baptiste
introduced.how: the novelist who grows the rare rose and confesses to being the murderer
introduced.quote: I will confess. I was the killer.

introduced.name: Fortress of Meropide
introduced.how: a prison where a wealthy convict could still live comfortably
introduced.quote: I bet he could lead an extremely comfortable life in the Fortress of Meropide.

introduced.name: The Two Musketeers
introduced.how: the film being shot, showing two sisters' final confrontation with the Baron
introduced.quote: Furina: This upcoming scene is the Two Musketeers' final confrontation with the baron.

introduced.name: Gardemeks
introduced.how: guard robots the novelist hired so he will not be harassed or disturbed
introduced.quote: According to what he told me the last time we spoke, he hired them so he won't be harassed or disturbed.

introduced.name: Baptiste's mother's murder
introduced.how: Baptiste's mother was killed twenty years ago by a hired assassin on the orders of his wealthy father
introduced.quote: But... I am indeed the illegitimate son of a wealthy and influential man, who abused his power to murder my mother. That part was a hundred percent real.

introduced.name: the true mastermind
introduced.how: Baptiste's wealthy father, the true mastermind behind his mother's death, who is still unpunished
introduced.quote: You still haven't managed to take revenge against your father, the true mastermind behind it all.

assumed.name: murder case
assumed.quote: But didn't you say that he had an alibi?

assumed.name: Yashiro Commission
assumed.quote: Unfortunately... there are still many matters that I have to take care of back home at the Yashiro Commission.

assumed.name: Special Security and Surveillance Patrol
assumed.quote: Don't forget, I'm the Captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol.

assumed.name: Marechaussee Phantom
assumed.quote: It will help the Marechaussee Phantom confirm Emilie's theory.

assumed.name: The Steambird
assumed.quote: We'll just keep an eye on The Steambird, then.

threads.claim: Chevreuse has learned the name of the true mastermind from Baptiste but withholds it from the Traveler and Paimon.
threads.quote: Chevreuse: Yes, he did. But for now, I have to return to the Special Patrol. There are still a few loose ends I need to tie up.

threads.claim: The Traveler suspects Chevreuse is keeping important information from the party.
threads.quote: Traveler: (What's going on? It feels like she's keeping something from us.)

threads.claim: Baptiste asks Chevreuse to kill the true mastermind on his behalf, since he cannot take revenge himself.
threads.quote: Baptiste: No, what I'd like is for you to perform the deed on my behalf.

threads.claim: Baptiste doubts that justice can reach his father and questions whether a comfortable prison sentence counts as justice.
threads.quote: Baptiste: Justice will never find him.

threads.claim: Baptiste's novel mixes fiction with real events from his own life, including his mother's murder.
threads.quote: Baptiste: No, of course not. It was a work of fiction with many embellished parts.

threads.claim: Emilie's expertise traces the killer's rose cultivar to the novelist's garden, the only place in Fontaine that grows it.
threads.quote: We already knew that the rose left at the scene belonged to a special cultivar, but with Emilie's expertise, we were able to pinpoint the place where it was first picked from.

threads.claim: Baptiste confesses to the murder, so his earlier alibi is broken and the killer is identified.
threads.quote: I will confess. I was the killer.

introduced.name: Alice
introduced.how: Mysterious telepathic voice who calls herself Durin's aunt and M's close friend
introduced.quote: Alice: Aw, no need to be shy. Just think of me as one of your mother's dearest friends.

introduced.name: Durin
introduced.how: Dragon-born youth raised by wolves, part dragon, and M's son
introduced.quote: Lisa: I figured, if I can handle a boy raised by wolves, then teaching one who's part dragon should be a walk in the park.

introduced.name: The Little Witch and the Undying Fire
introduced.how: Famous book that was written collaboratively by several mages
introduced.quote: Alice: That's because it was the work of more than one person.

introduced.name: Magic of storytelling
introduced.how: Storytelling magic was born when the writer and watcher met
introduced.quote: Alice: The day that the writer and the watcher crossed paths was the day that the magic known as storytelling was born.

introduced.name: Magic ink
introduced.how: M's ink infused with Alice's magic, required to write into the book and very scarce
introduced.quote: Alice: This, my dear little Paimon, is the ink M left behind — infused with a little of my own magic, of course.

introduced.name: Restricted section
introduced.how: The library has a sealed restricted section holding forbidden books
introduced.quote: Y'know, the first time you mentioned that the library had a "restricted section," Paimon thought you were just trying to scare us.

introduced.name: Experiment Log No. book
introduced.how: Forbidden alchemy book with formulas that can create dangerous monsters, brought in by Albedo
introduced.quote: Lisa: He said it's full of forbidden alchemical formulas, some of which could even result in the creation of dangerous monsters.

introduced.name: Second Strongest Spell in Existence book
introduced.how: Restricted book holding one of Alice's spells, sealed so Klee cannot read it
introduced.quote: Lisa: It's true, this book does contain one of Ms. Alice's spells.

introduced.name: Verses book
introduced.how: Banned poetry collection whose poem recasts the Dragonspine dragon as an innocent child
introduced.quote: Lisa: The issue lies with one of the poems inside.

introduced.name: Dragon's rampage and battle at Dragonspine
introduced.how: Five hundred years ago an evil dragon attacked Mondstadt during the Khaenri'ah cataclysm and was slain
introduced.quote: Lisa: Five hundred years ago, during the cataclysm in Khaenri'ah, an evil dragon descended upon Mondstadt.

introduced.name: Durin's dragon egg origin
introduced.how: Durin was created by a witch who wove a dragon egg from magic to raise a dragon-child
introduced.quote: With it she wove a dragon's egg, resolving to rear a dragon-child of her own.

introduced.name: Jumpy Dumpty Treasure Trove
introduced.how: A forbidden book written by Klee about fish-blasting spots and hiding Jumpy Dumpties
introduced.quote: Lisa: Because this is something Klee wrote.

introduced.name: The Boar Princess
introduced.how: A classic library book written by M
introduced.quote: Lisa: Well, this book has quite an obvious connection with that mage, considering she was the one who wrote it.

introduced.name: Durin (NPC)
introduced.how: Durin is the Traveler's companion, raised inside his mother's stories in Simulanka and new to the real world
introduced.quote: Durin: For as long as I can remember, I've spent most of my time living in the stories my mother created.

introduced.name: Barbatos
introduced.how: the wind god Venti is revealed as Lord Barbatos, a wandering bard who once sang the riddle verses to mages
introduced.quote: Venti: Long ago, those mages came to Mondstadt, seeking to test their strength against mine.

introduced.name: Hexenzirkel
introduced.how: the witches of the story are the mages of the Hexenzirkel, a group that gathers at a shared table
introduced.quote: Paimon: Those witches in the story were the mages of the Hexenzirkel, right? They sure seemed to care a lot about you, Durin!

introduced.name: Hexenzirkel's Island in the Sky
introduced.how: the mages made this location their official meeting spot after Venti's riddle was solved
introduced.quote: Venti: You should know, after solving my riddle, the mages even accepted my proposal, and made that location their official meeting spot.

introduced.name: Simulanka
introduced.how: the storybook world that is a major part of Durin's past and story
introduced.quote: Paimon: Yeah, Simulanka is a big part of Durin's story. So, guess it's no surprise the people we were with there would make an appearance.

introduced.name: Dvalin
introduced.how: the dragon living in Mondstadt, described as a magnificent creature Durin hopes to meet
introduced.quote: Durin: I've heard that the dragon here is called Dvalin, and that he's a magnificent creature. I hope I get the chance to meet him.

introduced.name: Stormterror's Lair
introduced.how: a real-world dragon habitat in Mondstadt where the story clue points
introduced.quote: Durin: I asked around, and it just so happens that there's a place like that in Mondstadt.

introduced.name: M
introduced.how: Durin's mother, the story-witch whose pen wrote the story of Simulanka
introduced.quote: Paimon: So this is M's pen? The one she used to write the story of Simulanka? You must know it well, Durin...

introduced.name: Alice
introduced.how: the merry-witch of the story, revealed to be the creator-goddess of the storybook realm
introduced.quote: Paimon: Alice? Wait, you're the "merry-witch" from the story?

introduced.name: Goddess of Fate
introduced.how: the story-witch is the Goddess of Fate, as stated by the merry-witch
introduced.quote: Merry-Witch: Hahaha, correct! It is I, the merry-witch, creator-goddess of this realm. And it just so happens, the Goddess of Fate is none other than my dear friend, the story-witch.

introduced.name: Mini Durin
introduced.how: a storybook version of Durin, the dragon-child, who is brought to life by the witch's ink
introduced.quote: Traveler: It's the storybook Durin.

introduced.name: witch's pen
introduced.how: the pen of the story-witch, the source of the tales, that Durin's mother used to write
introduced.quote: Narrator: What the guests saw before them was none other than the witch's pen, the source of countless moving tales.

introduced.name: Abyssal power
introduced.how: a dangerous power inside Durin that is becoming unstable
introduced.quote: Kaeya: Worse still, the Abyssal power within him is showing signs of extreme instability. Could be a separate issue, though. I'm not sure.

introduced.name: Mondstadt forgetting Durin
introduced.how: most people of Mondstadt have forgotten Durin, except his close acquaintances
introduced.quote: Kaeya: It seems like... aside from Durin's close acquaintances, the people of Mondstadt have forgotten everything about him.

introduced.name: Durin's evil dragon past
introduced.how: Durin was once the evil dragon that fell on Dragonspine, which some townsfolk remember
introduced.quote: Marjorie: Excuse me, did I hear you call him "Durin" just now? But, wasn't Durin the evil dragon that fell on Dragonspine?

introduced.name: prophecy of the evil dragon's fate
introduced.how: the seer-witch foretells that a child bearing the evil dragon's name inherits its fate
introduced.quote: Seer-Witch: His fate... has been foretold.

introduced.name: Genius Invokation TCG
introduced.how: a card game Durin learns as a non-alcoholic way to make friends
introduced.quote: Durin: But, that's why I started learning how to play Genius Invokation TCG. It's also a kind of social activity, but it doesn't involve drinking.

introduced.name: Durin (NPC)
introduced.how: Simulanka dragon whose body holds sealed abyssal power and who is now being forgotten by the world
introduced.quote: Abyssal power lies sealed within this body I inhabit, so when I lost my connection to it, I lost control of that power too...

introduced.name: Simulanka
introduced.how: a place where a heartfelt wish can rewrite the cruelest fate, unlike Teyvat
introduced.quote: it's a place where a heartfelt wish is all it takes to rewrite the cruelest fate... Not like here, where fate mocks us all.

introduced.name: Seer-Witch
introduced.how: a prophetess who gives the little dragon a prophecy; described as Mona's teacher
introduced.quote: I am the seer-witch, your prophetess — not some old hag!

introduced.name: Mini Durin
introduced.how: the storybook version of Durin who appears inside the tale as a little dragon
introduced.quote: It's the storybook Durin...

introduced.name: Hat Guy
introduced.how: Durin's Simulanka friend who wrote a travelogue about their time there, and who is the Traveler's nickname in Durin's eyes
introduced.quote: If I remember correctly, Hat Guy loved the time he spent in Simulanka so much that he started writing a travelogue.

introduced.name: Katayoun
introduced.how: a Sumeru library staffer who enforces the catalog and loan protocols
introduced.quote: Sir, you have to understand... managing a library is a serious business and we have protocols in place for this kind of thing.

introduced.name: Flip Back
introduced.how: a feature of the book that lets the reader turn back the pages after a bad ending
introduced.quote: I built a very special feature into this book — just for you, the witnesses of this tale.

introduced.name: Bad End
introduced.how: an ending the story can reach that is written onto Durin and is problematic to trigger
introduced.quote: So be careful, because triggering a bad ending could be somewhat... problematic.

introduced.name: storytelling
introduced.how: a magic given to the world by the gods that governs how people meet, grow close, and understand one another, and gives each person a fated story
introduced.quote: Long, long ago, the gods of the high heavens gave the world outside the castle a magic of its own.

introduced.name: mirror fates
introduced.how: Simulanka Durin and Teyvat Durin have fates that are mirror images of one another
introduced.quote: Simulanka Durin and Teyvat Durin share a special kind of connection: their fates are mirror images of one another.

introduced.name: Ley Lines
introduced.how: the world's ley lines do not affect Durin and are rejecting his existence
introduced.quote: The fact is, you're not affected by the Ley Lines of this world.

introduced.name: The Durin
introduced.how: a paper boat from Durin and Hat Guy's Simulanka adventures that can fly
introduced.quote: Of course, and it can even fly! Back in Simulanka, me and my friends used to be able to hop on and get almost anywhere in no time.

introduced.name: Sumeru City
introduced.how: a city with a huge library, the next place to search for the answer
introduced.quote: Think about it — our search in Mondstadt began in a library, right? Well, Sumeru City's got one of those too, and it's absolutely huge!

introduced.name: evil dragon of Dragonspine
introduced.how: the evil dragon that fell on Dragonspine, whose tale now fills the remaining records about Durin
introduced.quote: about the evil dragon that fell on Dragonspine.

introduced.name: seer-witch's prophecy
introduced.how: a prophecy that the dragon from beyond the castle will be reborn and cannot be averted
introduced.quote: Hear me now, for my prophecy is this: one day, the dragon from beyond the castle shall be reborn, and none may avert its coming.

introduced.name: Durin (NPC)
introduced.how: a storybook dragon written from his mother's tale, brought into Teyvat to replace the Dragonspine Durin
introduced.quote: Albedo: Bringing fairytale Durin into this world to replace the Durin on Dragonspine means using one Durin's fate to overwrite the other's.

introduced.name: Anya "Marie" Andersdotter
introduced.how: Durin's mother, a storybook writer who died long ago, whose voice survives as a magical echo
introduced.quote: Anya: My child, I... or your mother, I should say, passed away long ago.

introduced.name: Barbatos
introduced.how: Venti is revealed to be the Anemo Archon, Barbatos
introduced.quote: Durin: Sorry for the trouble, Lord Barbatos...

introduced.name: Hexenzirkel
introduced.how: a circle of witches who run risky experiments and gather at a sky tea party
introduced.quote: The scene shifts to the Hexenzirkel's tea party in the sky, where they gather as Dodocos

introduced.name: Simulanka
introduced.how: the storybook world Durin came from
introduced.quote: Durin: I'm starting to think I kinda miss being in Simulanka...

introduced.name: Abyss
introduced.how: a dark power inside Durin's body that can take over if his will fades
introduced.quote: Albedo: The issue isn't so much that the Abyssal power within him has gotten out of control.

introduced.name: Story ink
introduced.how: a magical ink made from finished stories, which lets Durin continue writing his own tale
introduced.quote: Anya: But I've found a way to use your magic to transform some of my finished stories into a special kind of ink.

introduced.name: Evil dragon's heart
introduced.how: the still-beating heart of a long-dead evil dragon, which the story's dark power is tied to
introduced.quote: What the clay figure found was none other than the evil dragon's heart itself.

introduced.name: Storyless void
introduced.how: an unwritten chapter of the story that cannot be entered
introduced.quote: Narrator: Ahead of them was a storyless void, and they could go no further.

introduced.name: Fate
introduced.how: the fate of every living being in Teyvat is woven into time, and is distinct from a being's story
introduced.quote: As Miss Barbeloth reminded us, the fate of every living being in Teyvat has been woven into the fabric of time.

introduced.name: Story magic
introduced.how: a magic that takes over writing a story after its author is gone
introduced.quote: Alice: I could create a kind of "story magic" to take over the writing once you're gone.

introduced.name: Pen
introduced.how: Anya's pen, which carries the power to write the story and is passed to Durin
introduced.quote: I would like you to send this pen of mine into the future.

introduced.name: Barbeloth's prophecy
introduced.how: a prophecy of a foretold moment that is still centuries away
introduced.quote: Barbeloth: Exactly. And the moment foretold by the prophecy is still centuries away.

introduced.name: Alice's book
introduced.how: a magical book that records the story and its endings, which is returned to Alice
introduced.quote: Alice: Congratulations on completing your mission! Now then, as per our agreement, it's about time you returned that book.

assumed.name: Lisa
assumed.quote: Lisa: Well, it has been far too long since we saw each other, so I suppose I can let it slide just this once...

assumed.name: Venti
assumed.quote: The Traveler immediately realizes that Venti might know the answer just as Durin notices Anemo energy pointing their way to him.

assumed.name: Kaeya
assumed.quote: They arrive at Good Hunter, where they find Durin playing against Kaeya in a game of Genius Invokation TCG.

assumed.name: Klee
assumed.quote: Paimon: Well, it wouldn't be Klee's mom without a hefty dose of mystery, huh? Let's go see what this is about.

assumed.name: Jean
assumed.quote: Lisa: Back when he first arrived here. Poor Jean wasn't sure what to do with him, so I stepped in to lend a hand.

assumed.name: Albedo
assumed.quote: Durin is confident that his brother wouldn't have had made a mistake.

assumed.name: Dvalin
assumed.quote: As they leave, Venti and Dvalin watch them from afar, the former telling the latter that they wanted to be friends.

assumed.name: Simulanka
assumed.quote: Paimon: Whoa, what is this place? It reminds Paimon of Simulanka...

assumed.name: Hexenzirkel
assumed.quote: Paimon: All the people we've seen that looked like that turned out to be mages from the Hexenzirkel.

assumed.name: Good Hunter
assumed.quote: Paimon: Yeah, Paimon has a sudden craving for the Good Hunter's Sticky Honey Roast...

assumed.name: Mondstadt Library
assumed.quote: Paimon: Back in the Mondstadt Library, huh? Talk about a trip down memory lane!

assumed.name: Wanderer
assumed.quote: They then explore the story, finding that it appears to emulate the path he had taken after leaving Simulanka.

assumed.name: Irminsul
assumed.quote: As a Descender unaffected by Irminsul's changes, he believes that the world refuses to accept the Durin before them as a separate entity

assumed.name: Barbeloth
assumed.quote: He explains that the witches had a plan to allow Durin to live, requiring the use of Barbeloth's astrology, Rhinedottir's alchemy and Alice's magic.

assumed.name: Rhinedottir
assumed.quote: He explains that the witches had a plan to allow Durin to live, requiring the use of Barbeloth's astrology, Rhinedottir's alchemy and Alice's magic.

assumed.name: Katayoun
assumed.quote: The clues lead them to Sumeru City, where they find the Wanderer returning a modified book to Katayoun.

assumed.name: Abyssal power
assumed.quote: Traveler: Is the Abyssal power inside you acting up?

assumed.name: Albedo
assumed.quote: Durin: Albedo introduced us when I first arrived in Mondstadt. I mean, someone like me was bound to catch his eye sooner or later.

assumed.name: Klee
assumed.quote: Traveler: I'm guessing... Klee took you fish blasting?

assumed.name: Kaeya
assumed.quote: Kaeya: Not every day you're back in Mondstadt, huh? Care to grab a drink, if you're free?

assumed.name: Diona
assumed.quote: Paimon: Oh, Diona stepped in! Y'know, underneath it all, she really does like helping people.

assumed.name: Lisa
assumed.quote: Durin: A musical performance, huh... Out of all the things Miss Lisa has taught me, that's the one I'm worst at...

assumed.name: Fischl
assumed.quote: Fischl: So be it... Such are fate's accursed wiles. Hmph!

assumed.name: Dodoco
assumed.quote: Klee: Don't be sad, Durin! You'll definitely win the next round. You can even borrow Dodoco, if you want. Mom says she brings good luck!

assumed.name: Hat Guy
assumed.quote: Durin: Oh, and there's Hat Guy too. Only...

assumed.name: Nod-Krai
assumed.quote: Durin: If my time in Nod-Krai taught me anything, it's that a lot of problems in this world can only be settled by strength of arms.

assumed.name: Constellation Metropole
assumed.quote: Durin: I always thought my mother had everything written out for me already — just like the toy figures in Constellation Metropole.

assumed.name: Nilou, Navia and Kirara
assumed.quote: Durin: Yeah... Like the fairy from the Forest of Blessings, the King of Constellation Metropole, that cat lady who turns into a box...

assumed.name: Alice
assumed.quote: That means we need Alice for sure... But it's been ages and she still hasn't been in contact...

assumed.name: Albedo
assumed.quote: Sounds like we need Albedo more than ever...

assumed.name: Mona
assumed.quote: Ohhh yeah, that's Mona's teacher, right?

assumed.name: Jean
assumed.quote: Hello, you two! I'm glad you got my letter.

assumed.name: Lisa, Kaeya, and Klee
assumed.quote: (Jean leads them over to Lisa, Kaeya, and Klee)

assumed.name: Mondstadt library hunt
assumed.quote: After the library hunt in Mondstadt, it's not as if Paimon was expecting this to be easy.

assumed.name: Nod-Krai
assumed.quote: Well, the last time we saw you was all the way in Nod-Krai.

assumed.name: Irminsul
assumed.quote: Irminsul...

assumed.name: Flying Squirrel Fairy, Giraffe King, and Cat in a Box
assumed.quote: Hello again, golden-haired traveler and silver pixie.

assumed.name: Alice
assumed.quote: Paimon: So the reason Alice had us complete this book... was to make that magic possible?

assumed.name: Barbeloth
assumed.quote: It would have required the combined use of Miss Barbeloth's astrology, my teacher's alchemy, and Aunt Alice's magic.

assumed.name: Jean
assumed.quote: Albedo: Master Jean filled me in on what happened, and I've got a few theories, but let's get on the same page first.

assumed.name: Wanderer
assumed.quote: (The Wanderer patters over in his kitten form)

assumed.name: Mondstadt dragon revival
assumed.quote: If this had been the dragon that ended up being revived in Mondstadt, there's no telling what kind of calamity the people would have had to endure.

assumed.name: Mini Durin
assumed.quote: Paimon: Hey, it's Mini Durin again! What are you doing holed up in here?

assumed.name: Venti
assumed.quote: Paimon: Eh? What are you doing here, Tone-Deaf Bard?

assumed.name: Knights of Favonius
assumed.quote: Paimon: Hey, a letter from the Knights of Favonius! Sounds like Albedo's back, and he's waiting for us on Dragonspine!

threads.claim: Durin's abyssal power is becoming harder to control, hinting at a looming danger.
threads.quote: Durin: Hmm... I don't know, it just feels like it's gotten harder to control.

threads.claim: Durin's symptoms are gone after the ordeal, so the abyssal danger is resolved.
threads.quote: Albedo checks up on him again and notes that the previous symptoms were no longer there, and they decide to celebrate with a party

threads.claim: M's greatest regret was leaving a story unfinished, and her final wish is a mystery.
threads.quote: Alice: And that is the answer to my question. A writer's greatest regret is to leave a story unfinished.

threads.claim: Paimon questions why M believes the story is still unfinished despite Durin's happy ending.
threads.quote: Paimon: Yeah, but why does "M" seem to think that the story isn't finished yet?

threads.claim: The book keeps giving clues, so the story is not yet finished.
threads.quote: He then reveals that the book continued giving clues, indicating that their story is not yet finished.

threads.claim: Durin is promised a different fate from the evil dragon before him, raising the question of what fate awaits him.
threads.quote: Story-Witch: But I promise you this: your birth was wanted, you are loved, and you will have a different fate than the dragon that came before you.

threads.claim: The banned poem's version of the Dragonspine battle may be false, and only the dragon knows the truth.
threads.quote: Lisa: ...I'm afraid that question is something only the dragon himself could answer.

threads.claim: Durin's story keeps reverting to the evil Durin recorded in history, and the world resists him as a separate being.
threads.quote: The Wanderer reveals that whenever he tried to write about Durin, it would inexplicably change to the Durin recorded in history.

threads.claim: Alice's forbidden spell and alchemy books are sealed away, hinting at dangerous secrets.
threads.quote: Lisa: The only reason it's even meant to be in the restricted section is because we can't let Klee get her hands on it.

threads.claim: The magic ink is scarce and must be used sparingly to write into the book.
threads.quote: Alice: It's extremely precious, so be sure to use it sparingly. This is all that's left.

threads.claim: Durin is driven to fulfill his mother's final wish, which he fears he might ruin.
threads.quote: Durin: Hm... Maybe I'm overthinking things. It's just, this is my mother's final wish, so I don't want to mess it up.

threads.claim: The mother's final story comes to a close after the little dragon's wish is granted.
threads.quote: Durin: So, my mother's final story has finally come to a close...

threads.claim: The seer-witch says the child's fate has already been foretold because of the evil dragon's name.
threads.quote: Seer-Witch: His fate... has been foretold.

threads.claim: The little dragon grows claws and scales of an evil dragon, as the prophecy foretold.
threads.quote: But already, he had grown the claws and scales of an evil dragon, just as the prophecy had foretold.

threads.claim: The little dragon's curse is lifted when the wish to the Goddess of Fate is granted.
threads.quote: At last, their wish was granted. Shaking off his scales, the little dragon stepped out of the tower's gloom.

threads.claim: The story-witch vows to rewrite the child's fate despite the prophecy.
threads.quote: Story-Witch: ...Then I'll rewrite it.

threads.claim: With the blessings of the witches, the dragon-child's fate begins to turn.
threads.quote: Narrator: With the witches' blessings given and received, the little dragon's fate at last began to turn.

threads.claim: Mondstadt's people seem to have forgotten Durin, a sudden and unexplained event.
threads.quote: Kaeya: Did everyone just... forget about Durin?

threads.claim: Only Durin's close acquaintances still remember him, and the cause is unknown.
threads.quote: Kaeya: It seems like... aside from Durin's close acquaintances, the people of Mondstadt have forgotten everything about him.

threads.claim: Durin's Abyssal power is becoming unstable and could threaten Mondstadt.
threads.quote: Kaeya: Worse still, the Abyssal power within him is showing signs of extreme instability. Could be a separate issue, though. I'm not sure.

threads.claim: Jean requests Albedo's immediate return to help with Durin's situation.
threads.quote: Jean: Alright then. As Acting Grand Master, I'll send a letter requesting Albedo's immediate return. Until then, the Knights will watch over Durin.

threads.claim: Alice has not yet contacted the Traveler's party, leaving the book's purpose unclear.
threads.quote: Paimon: It's just weird that Alice still hasn't contacted us... Maybe we should head back inside the book and take another look.

threads.claim: The Traveler suggests that Alice can be consulted if trouble arises.
threads.quote: Traveler: Even if we run into trouble, we can always go ask Alice.

threads.claim: Durin hopes to meet Dvalin, a dragon he has only heard about.
threads.quote: Durin: I've heard that the dragon here is called Dvalin, and that he's a magnificent creature. I hope I get the chance to meet him.

threads.claim: Venti says the moment for Dvalin and Durin to meet has not yet come.
threads.quote: Venti: But the moment hasn't come, at least not yet. In any case, the story should have a better ending this time, don't you think?

threads.claim: Durin asks why an author would consider a story unfinished, a question tied to his mother's story.
threads.quote: Durin: Yeah, um... You must have read countless tales in your time, being a wandering bard and all. In your experience, why might an author consider a story "unfinished"?

threads.claim: Venti says the answer lies in the mother's story itself.
threads.quote: Venti: In all seriousness, I would think, the answer to that question lies in your mother's story itself. It's not my place to pry any further.

threads.claim: Almost half the witches are absent from their gatherings, hinting at their unexplained absence.
threads.quote: Story-Witch: As rare a chance to gather as this, and yet almost half of us are absent...

threads.claim: The tricksy-witch controls the snowy lands and the wander-witch is still among the stars.
threads.quote: Merry-Witch: As of late, the tricksy-witch has nearly the entirety of the snowy lands in her grasp. Now, none but the Tsar can command her submission.

threads.claim: Hat Guy seems to be hiding something on his mind that Durin senses.
threads.quote: Durin: It's like... there's something on his mind. He hasn't told me what it is, but I can sense it all the same.

threads.claim: Durin says he had never expected to make friends until the Traveler's party came, and the blessings theme grows.
threads.quote: Durin: Before I met you all, I was so sure I'd never make a single friend.

threads.claim: The Traveler wonders whether the storybook is connected to the events in the real world.
threads.quote: Paimon: Do you think... the book might have something to do with what's happening?

threads.claim: The world is gradually forgetting Durin, and even his friends in Mondstadt are starting to lose track of him.
threads.quote: I'm fine now, it's just... a lot of people seem to have forgotten me.

threads.claim: Records of Durin vanish whenever his name is mentioned, and the forgetting is spreading to people who never knew him well.
threads.quote: before long, the record would disappear.

threads.claim: Abyssal power is sealed inside Durin's body and can slip out of control when his connection to the body is lost.
threads.quote: Abyssal power lies sealed within this body I inhabit, so when I lost my connection to it, I lost control of that power too...

threads.claim: Durin is unaffected by the Ley Lines, which suggests the world itself is rejecting his existence.
threads.quote: The fact is, you're not affected by the Ley Lines of this world.

threads.claim: Only people who still remember Durin keep him tied to this world, so losing them could be catastrophic.
threads.quote: With the Ley Lines rejecting him like this, the people who still remember him are his only remaining connection to this place.

threads.claim: Simulanka Durin and Teyvat Durin cannot both exist, because the rules of this world do not allow two fates at once.
threads.quote: The answer is, they can't. The rules of this world don't allow it.

threads.claim: Storytelling is a fate-binding magic that cannot tolerate two versions of the same tale, which explains why Durin's story cannot take root beyond the castle.
threads.quote: Long, long ago, the gods of the high heavens gave the world outside the castle a magic of its own.

threads.claim: Alice's recorded voice reveals she wrote Durin's experiences into the book and built its features on purpose, but she is still not directly reachable.
threads.quote: You may have noticed that little Durin's experiences have been written into the pages of this book.

threads.claim: The book lets the reader flip back to an earlier point after reaching a bad ending and replay the tale.
threads.quote: If you're not happy with the ending you've reached, just flip back a few pages and let the tale unfold once more.

threads.claim: Reaching a bad ending has consequences that affect Durin directly, not just the reader.
threads.quote: So be careful, because triggering a bad ending could be somewhat... problematic.

threads.claim: The prophecy says the dragon from beyond the castle will be reborn, and the wind is guiding the little dragon toward its fulfillment.
threads.quote: Hear me now, for my prophecy is this: one day, the dragon from beyond the castle shall be reborn, and none may avert its coming.

threads.claim: The evil dragon's tale has overwritten the records of Durin, and the evil dragon's story may be taking over his fate.
threads.quote: about the evil dragon that fell on Dragonspine.

threads.claim: The Traveler suspects that Durin's forgetting may come from spending too much time with him, possibly a curse like the one the stray cat carries.
threads.quote: When I first realized you were being forgotten by the world, I thought it might be because you'd spent too much time with me.

threads.claim: The Traveler concludes that the suspicion was overthinking, and that cutting ties would not be the cure.
threads.quote: Judging from the answer this book has given us, I was probably overthinking it.

threads.claim: The Traveler is planning something big that they have not yet revealed.
threads.quote: And considering what I'm planning to do next, it feels like a weight off my shoulders...

threads.claim: The Traveler believes the world's fate is controlled by a spiteful being, and defies it instead of accepting it.
threads.quote: If there really is a being controlling the fate of this world, it must be a laughably spiteful creature, deaf to the wishes of others.

threads.claim: The paper boat from Durin's Simulanka adventures flies even though the story says paper boats cannot fly beyond the castle.
threads.quote: In the world beyond the castle, no paper boat had ever flown before.

threads.claim: Durin's will is fading and the Abyssal power in his body threatens to take over.
threads.quote: Albedo: The issue isn't so much that the Abyssal power within him has gotten out of control. It's that the connection between his will and body is fading.

threads.claim: Durin's Abyssal power is stabilized and his symptoms are gone.
threads.quote: The Abyssal power within you has stabilized again, and those strange symptoms you were experiencing seem to have completely disappeared.

threads.claim: Durin is being forgotten by others even after his memory is restored.
threads.quote: Albedo: If that really was the solution, though, this would have been over the minute I finished the transmutation. So why is Durin still being forgotten?

threads.claim: Durin's fading connection to the world causes people to forget him and loses him control of the Abyssal power.
threads.quote: As Durin's connection to this world wore thin, not only have people started to forget him, he's started to lose control of the Abyssal power within.

threads.claim: A being's story differs fundamentally from its fate.
threads.quote: But there is a fundamental difference between a being's "story" and its "fate."

threads.claim: A story needs an author to keep writing it, unlike fate, which simply runs along its track.
threads.quote: Traveler: Needs an author...

threads.claim: The author can only leave a limited number of words behind, while the world keeps changing.
threads.quote: Alice: No matter how much you write, there is a limit to the number of words you can leave behind, but the world itself will never stop changing.

threads.claim: Durin might burn through the ink and get stuck roaming the chapters of his past.
threads.quote: Alice: It's entirely possible he burns through all your ink, never reaches the chapter you had in mind, and gets stuck roaming the chapters of his past.

threads.claim: Anya entrusts Durin with the ink so he can write his own story.
threads.quote: Anya: And so, by leaving him this ink, I can entrust him with the responsibility of writing his own story.

threads.claim: The evil dragon's heart is still alive and will return one day.
threads.quote: Narrator: And the clay alchemist knew what it meant — that the evil dragon would return one day, just as the prophecy had foretold.

threads.claim: The heart's roots remain buried, so destroying its branches does not kill it.
threads.quote: But the evil dragon's heart was like a great tree with roots digging deep beneath the surface.

threads.claim: The prophecy holds true, and the little dragon is reborn as foretold.
threads.quote: Thus did the prophecy hold true, even as fate had been rewritten — and so was the little dragon born anew.

threads.claim: Some magic may be able to influence the fate of Teyvat, and the answer lies in the book.
threads.quote: Albedo: I still can't figure out how any kind of magic could possibly influence the fate of Teyvat, but I'm certain that the answer lies within this book.

threads.claim: Durin defeats the darkness and rewrites his fate.
threads.quote: And so it was that Durin defeated the darkness and rewrote his fate.

threads.claim: Durin's mother Anya has already died, and her voice is an echo.
threads.quote: Anya: My child, I... or your mother, I should say, passed away long ago.

threads.claim: Anya passes her pen to Durin before her voice fades.
threads.quote: Anya: Take my pen and use it to continue your story

threads.claim: Players can flip back through the book to retry the story after a bad ending.
threads.quote: Alice: If you're not happy with the ending you've reached, just flip back a few pages and let the tale unfold once more.

threads.claim: Durin is a storybook character written into being by an author called "M".
threads.quote: Albedo: Durin was — and still is, in essence — a storybook character written into being by "M." From the moment he was born, he has always dwelt within her story.

threads.claim: Durin's mother has already left him her parting words through "M".
threads.quote: "M": There's no need. His mother already did that, long, long ago.

introduced.name: Shion
introduced.how: A baku who treats patients at a clinic and digests nightmare fragments to clear them
introduced.quote: The baku have been fasting all night, so we should be able to get rid of this nightmare no problem.

introduced.name: Popcorn
introduced.how: Homura's childhood imaginary friend, separated from her and now visible to others
introduced.quote: Popcorn: Well, actually... Homura is all grown up now...

introduced.name: Homura
introduced.how: A grown-up former child, overworked at her first job, who once had Popcorn as an imaginary friend
introduced.quote: Homura: But, this is already the 12th draft... *sigh* Never mind. Understood.

introduced.name: Prune
introduced.how: A Witch Hunter who joins the Little Hexenzirkel and whose imaginary friend Descartes was taken
introduced.quote: Prune: I'm a Witch Hunter. Witches are my enemies!

introduced.name: Descartes
introduced.how: Prune's imaginary friend, a purple puppy, who was taken away and returns
introduced.quote: Descartes is my best friend...

introduced.name: Alice
introduced.how: A powerful witch who staged the challenge and the imaginary-friend plot, and is Klee's mother
introduced.quote: Alice: I just thought I'd give all our lovely imaginary friends a chance to come out and say hello.

introduced.name: Little Hexenzirkel
introduced.how: A group of child witches led by Klee that Prune joins; founded at a young age
introduced.quote: Founding the Little Hexenzirkel at such a young age

introduced.name: Witch Hunters
introduced.how: An organization whose members see witches as enemies
introduced.quote: Prune: I'm a Witch Hunter. Witches are my enemies!

introduced.name: nightmare fragments
introduced.how: Shards left by nightmares that baku can consume to free a person from them
introduced.quote: Traveler: These are the fragments we collected.

introduced.name: mental escapism
introduced.how: Fantasizing about happiness as an adult becomes self-deception; real change requires action
introduced.quote: But adults know it isn't real, so imagination becomes a form of self-deception. It's called a mental escapade.

introduced.name: imaginary friends
introduced.how: Normally they live inside a child's head, but they can appear in the real world
introduced.quote: Aren't imaginary friends supposed to live inside kids' heads?

assumed.name: Aisa Bathhouse
assumed.quote: Isn't that the girl we met outside of Aisa Bathhouse a few days ago?

assumed.name: Dodoco
assumed.quote: But then, Dodoco reminds me that's a sure-fire way to get sent back to confinement

assumed.name: Dough King
assumed.quote: Qiqi: But the Dough King said you still have mental issues.

assumed.name: Master Jean
assumed.quote: even Master Jean can't catch me!

assumed.name: Mondstadt
assumed.quote: I went to Mondstadt to find them, only for the trail to lead me to Inazuma.

assumed.name: Yuegui
assumed.quote: A Dodoco, a finch, a huge mujina, and Yuegui appear around them

assumed.name: Tuantuan
assumed.quote: Qiqi: Tuantuan flew away... She wants to go play over there.

assumed.name: Sayu's sensei
assumed.quote: I'm trying to become an even stronger ninja than my sensei too.

threads.claim: Imaginary friends normally live inside children's heads and may fade as the child grows up.
threads.quote: Aren't imaginary friends supposed to live inside kids' heads?

threads.claim: Descartes was on the verge of disappearing before Alice intervened, so his fate is tied to Prune's growing up.
threads.quote: Alice: In fact, when I met little Prune, her imaginary friend was on the verge of disappearing.

threads.claim: Prune regained her childlike innocence through the group and reunited with her imaginary friend.
threads.quote: Alice: After spending time with the little witches, she regained her childlike innocence and was able to reunite with her imaginary friend.

threads.claim: Alice reportedly won a debate and took Prune's imaginary friend away, sending Prune to fight witches.
threads.quote: She challenged me to a debate, and when she lost, she took my imaginary friend away

threads.claim: Alice admits she invented the capture of Descartes and sent Prune to Mondstadt to help her.
threads.quote: Alice: Hah! That's why I made up the whole thing about capturing Descartes and sent her to Mondstadt

threads.claim: Patients who lose their sense of wonder may feel they can never regain their inner child.
threads.quote: it's the knowledge that my inner child is never coming back.

threads.claim: Alice argues children are pushed into adult life too soon and their innocence breaks as a result.
threads.quote: Alice: But it's unfair to expect a child to step into the adult world so soon.

threads.claim: Homura was freed from the nightmare but remains emotionally numb, so the problem is not fully solved.
threads.quote: Homura is free from the nightmare, but her psychological state is still abnormal...

threads.claim: Imagination and spirit are said to be best nurtured by freedom, which is why Alice chose Mondstadt.
threads.quote: Alice: Ah, well, the seeds of spirit and imagination are best nurtured by the soil of freedom, of course.

threads.claim: Klee is Alice's daughter, which complicates Prune's view of Alice as an enemy.
threads.quote: Prune: But... Klee is Alice's daughter...

threads.claim: Prune's Witch Hunter identity puts her at odds with the child witches she is drawn to.
threads.quote: Prune: I'm a Witch Hunter. Witches are my enemies!

threads.claim: Prune concludes the child witches are not evil and cannot be treated as enemies.
threads.quote: Prune: You're not evil witches at all, just a group of innocent kids...

threads.claim: Popcorn can be seen even though he is back to normal, which suggests an outside magic is involved.
threads.quote: Traveler: Popcorn's back to normal, but we can still see him...

threads.claim: Alice reveals that her magic let all the imaginary friends appear in the real world for a reunion.
threads.quote: Alice: I just thought I'd give all our lovely imaginary friends a chance to come out and say hello.

threads.claim: Alice says embracing one's inner child is the magic that brings happiness.
threads.quote: Alice: It's through embracing our inner child that all of us can wield the magic known as happiness.

introduced.name: Razor
introduced.how: a wolf-raised boy with a claymore who introduces himself and says he is no knight
introduced.quote: Razor: I am Razor.

introduced.name: Wolvendom
introduced.how: a wild area near Mondstadt, rarely visited by its people and ruled by nature's laws
introduced.quote: Paimon: This is Wolvendom. People from Mondstadt hardly ever come here...

introduced.name: Boreas
introduced.how: the Wolf of the North, who is enraged by the disturbance and demands Razor prove his worth
introduced.quote: Boreas, the Wolf of the North, is enraged by the disturbance and orders Razor to fight him to prove his worth for protecting outsiders.

introduced.name: Lupical
introduced.how: a bond where a wolf accepts a human as its own, or a human accepts a wolf, and Razor's name for it
introduced.quote: Razor: Lupical is family fate gave me. When wolf accepts human as its own. Or human accepts wolf. That is Lupical.

introduced.name: Wolfhook
introduced.how: a berry whose seeds have small hooks that let them cling to animals and spread far
introduced.quote: Amber: It's the seed of a Wolfhook berry. Look, there are little hooks on the seed.

introduced.name: Amber
introduced.how: a Knights of Favonius Outrider who investigates the wolf attacks and wants the Traveler's help
introduced.quote: An Outrider's duties never end, so... Wanna help?

introduced.name: Siegfria
introduced.how: a traveling merchant whose cart was hit by hilichurls and wolves on the road
introduced.quote: Siegfria: I thought I would take my chances on the road after the wolves had their fun...

introduced.name: Hopkins the Marvelous
introduced.how: a Springvale villager who accuses Razor of helping wolves plot against humans
introduced.quote: I can't believe you would help wolves plot against humans!

assumed.name: Knights of Favonius
assumed.quote: Paimon: Are you one of the Knights of Favonius too?

assumed.name: Mondstadt City
assumed.quote: At Mondstadt's front gate, the Traveler finds Amber and asks if they met Razor before.

assumed.name: Brightcrown Mountains
assumed.quote: Mondstadt's wolves don't normally venture outside of the Brightcrown Mountains and Wolvendom.

assumed.name: Drunkard Gorge
assumed.quote: Amber: I heard they attacked a cart fleet near Drunkard Gorge.

assumed.name: Liyue
assumed.quote: Amber: Wolf fur... I heard that in Liyue they make calligraphy brushes out of this stuff.

assumed.name: Hilichurls
assumed.quote: looks like it's the hilichurls attacking the carts after all.

threads.claim: A mysterious Guardian of this land gave wolves the name Lupical, and its identity is left open.
threads.quote: Razor: Guardian of this land.

threads.claim: A black wolf leading an outside pack is invading the land and breaking the wolves' code.
threads.quote: A black wolf and his pack, not from here. They try to take over land. They broke the code.

threads.claim: Boreas confirms that an outside wolf pack has been causing the attacks and will pay for it.
threads.quote: Boreas: It's just like he said. An outside wolf pack coming in and breaking the rules.

threads.claim: The fiery red girl Razor knows is someone other than Amber, and her identity remains unknown.
threads.quote: Razor: No. This girl is also red, but no so burny like other girl.

threads.claim: Lupical is explained as a bond in which a wolf accepts a human or a human accepts a wolf.
threads.quote: Razor: Lupical is family fate gave me. When wolf accepts human as its own. Or human accepts wolf. That is Lupical.

threads.claim: Razor is torn between human and wolf worlds, belonging fully to neither.
threads.quote: Razor: I am not like them! I don't belong.

threads.claim: A mysterious purple teacher has taught Razor knowledge about wolfhook seeds.
threads.quote: Razor: ...Purple teacher told me so.

threads.claim: Wolves follow their own rules and code of conduct that outsiders only partly understand.
threads.quote: Amber: As you know, wolves are dangerous, but they do have their own rules.

threads.claim: Amber still suspects Razor's pack of involvement in the attacks, leaving his innocence unproven.
threads.quote: Your wolf friend is not clear of my suspicion just yet.

threads.claim: Wolves that once stayed inside Wolvendom are now venturing outside and attacking people.
threads.quote: In the past, the wolves never dared venture outside of Wolvendom. But now they're getting braver.

introduced.name: Sabzeruz Festival
introduced.how: a festival tradition held in honor of Lesser Lord Kusanali's birthday, with set customs
introduced.quote: Dunyarzad: It's another Sabzeruz Festival tradition. People used to set their tables with seven different foods...

introduced.name: Haft-Mewa Feast
introduced.how: a tradition of setting tables with seven vegetarian foods such as mushrooms, lotuses, roses and fruits
introduced.quote: Dunyarzad: Generally speaking, the most common selections were foods like Rukkhashava Mushrooms, Nilotpala Lotuses, Sumeru Roses, Sunsettias, Kalpalatas, Harra Fruits, and Zaytun Peaches.

introduced.name: alchemical divination
introduced.how: a random transmutation of two reagents whose failed remnants a diviner interprets; said to be invented by Lesser Lord Kusanali
introduced.quote: Kimiya: Right? I thought the same when I first heard about it. It is said to be a mysterious craft invented by none other than Lesser Lord Kusanali herself.

introduced.name: Farris
introduced.how: the Knight of Flowers, a festival icon popular with children who was once played by an actor on a flower carriage
introduced.quote: Dunyarzad: Hehe. Farris, the Knight of Flowers, is another Sabzeruz Festival icon, and one immensely popular with children.

introduced.name: Eleazar
introduced.how: a terminal illness Dunyarzad was born with, which cannot be cured by Sumeru medicine and only slowed by environmental therapy
introduced.quote: Dunyarzad: I was actually... born with Eleazar. It's terminal now.

introduced.name: Akademiya
introduced.how: the body that holds legal authority over festivals in Sumeru, the only group allowed to host such events
introduced.quote: Setaria: The Sabzeruz Festival... The law also prohibits the private hosting of large-scale, religious festivals. Only the Akademiya can host such an event.

introduced.name: Azar
introduced.how: a Grand Sage of the Akademiya who shuts down the festival and bans public art performances
introduced.quote: Azar: Our Archon created the utopia that is Sumeru City for all scholars who sought validity, verity, and truth... while people like you wish to defile it.

introduced.name: Setaria
introduced.how: Azar's secretary who enforces the festival ban and speaks for the Akademiya's laws
introduced.quote: Setaria: ...Were you not aware that the law prohibits this type of performance from taking place without prior permission?

introduced.name: Dehya
introduced.how: a former mercenary known as the Flame-Mane who now serves as Dunyarzad's guardian and protector
introduced.quote: Badis: You're... Dehya!? Dehya the Flame-Mane... No wonder we mercs haven't heard anything about you for so long.

introduced.name: Homayani Family
introduced.how: Dunyarzad's family, the employer who hires Dehya and would pay a ransom for Dunyarzad
introduced.quote: Badis: Heh, that's right. We haven't received any of their Mora, but... I wonder how much the Homayanis would shell out to get you back?

introduced.name: Nahida
introduced.how: introduces herself as the mysterious figure guiding them through the loop
introduced.quote: Oh yeah, I'm Nahida.

introduced.name: Dehya
introduced.how: self-described professional mercenary trained in a martial school that stresses refined control
introduced.quote: I'm a professional fighter. My martial school has always emphasized the importance of refined control.

introduced.name: Dunyarzad
introduced.how: the real Dunyarzad is lying in bed, basically in a coma, and her illness is worsening
introduced.quote: Her condition's really bad, and she's basically in a coma.

introduced.name: Amal
introduced.how: a produce seller who gathers goods from the forest
introduced.quote: I picked all of these from the forest yesterday, so their freshness is guaranteed!

introduced.name: Vihar
introduced.how: a candy vendor whose children's Yalda Candy is sponsored by Dunyarzad
introduced.quote: Oh, are you interested in Yalda Candies? I have some boxes of candy here.

introduced.name: Kimiya
introduced.how: a diviner whose divinations are seen as accurate
introduced.quote: Was my divination so accurate that you felt compelled to compliment me in person?

introduced.name: Yalda Candies
introduced.how: boxed candies with random flavors, sold at the festival
introduced.quote: Oh, are you interested in Yalda Candies? I have some boxes of candy here.

introduced.name: Akasha
introduced.how: powered by a Gnosis, it compiles the wisdom of the populace and grants knowledge
introduced.quote: The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate, as it is the manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power.

introduced.name: Gnosis
introduced.how: the power source of the Akasha, here tied to Sumeru's Archon
introduced.quote: it's being powered by the Gnosis of Sumeru's Archon.

introduced.name: Akasha Terminal
introduced.how: a worn device linked to the Akasha that people can take off
introduced.quote: In that case, we should take off our Akasha Terminals right away!

introduced.name: Knowledge Capsule
introduced.how: a yellow capsule that restores lost memories and shows the mind the way
introduced.quote: the Knowledge Capsule was just your means of showing our minds the way

introduced.name: Samsara
introduced.how: a cycle in which the world loops, trapping everyone in a one-day samsara
introduced.quote: You, me, and everyone else are all stuck inside a one-day samsara...

introduced.name: Dendro
introduced.how: a blessing that gives the Traveler and Paimon heightened déjà vu and sensitivity
introduced.quote: You two received the blessing of Dendro, and you also have special, sensitive constitutions.

introduced.name: Dehya's new greatsword
introduced.how: a new weapon that oddly feels familiar in Dehya's hands
introduced.quote: if I had to say something, it's weird how such a new weapon could feel so familiar.

introduced.name: Lesser Lord Kusanali
introduced.how: Nahida is revealed to be Lesser Lord Kusanali
introduced.quote: Traveler: You are Lesser Lord Kusanali.

introduced.name: Akasha
introduced.how: A Gnosis-powered manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power that compiles wisdom and grants knowledge
introduced.quote: Nahida: The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate.

introduced.name: Dream harvesting
introduced.how: The Akasha keeps people's brains dreaming while separating their consciousness and harvesting their dreams
introduced.quote: Nahida: Correct. The Akasha is keeping each person's brain in a constant dream state, but also separating their consciousness from their own dream.

introduced.name: Sabzeruz samsara
introduced.how: The Sabzeruz Festival day repeats endlessly as a harvested dream
introduced.quote: Nahida: No one is any the wiser as another day passes in the dream, and so begins another samsara cycle...

introduced.name: Archon War
introduced.how: Described as a past conflict where gods fought over seven seats
introduced.quote: Nahida: Well, consider this, for all the horrors of the Archon War, at its heart, it was just a game where a bunch of gods fought over seven seats.

introduced.name: Dream host
introduced.how: The person whose mind generates a dream; they must realize they are dreaming to break the samsara
introduced.quote: Nahida: That means this dream belongs to a host who created it.

introduced.name: Puppet stand-ins
introduced.how: Azar and Setaria are puppets substituting for real people in the dream
introduced.quote: Traveler: They're puppets.

introduced.name: Nahida's origin
introduced.how: Nahida was found as a newborn after Rukkhadevata vanished and taken to Sumeru by the Sages
introduced.quote: Nahida: ...That story begins a long time ago. After Greater Lord Rukkhadevata disappeared, the Sages found my newly born self and took me back to Sumeru.

introduced.name: Katheryne's body as a puppet
introduced.how: Nahida borrows the bionic Snezhnayan puppet Katheryne through the Akasha
introduced.quote: When necessary, I just borrow this bionic Snezhnayan puppet.

introduced.name: First Sage tale
introduced.how: The First Sage was blessed by the Dendro Archon with a dream and later founded the Akademiya
introduced.quote: Nilou: Yeah, but have you heard the tale of the First Sage? To prevent a calamity, he went on a journey to find the Dendro Archon.

introduced.name: Dendro dream blessing
introduced.how: Only those blessed by Dendro gain dream-enhancing power, which explains déjà vu
introduced.quote: Nahida: Yes. Only after receiving the blessing of Dendro can a person gain the Dendro element's dream-enhancing power.

introduced.name: Vihar
introduced.how: Vihar is the Knight of Flowers role Dunyarzad gave him, and he has a crush on her
introduced.quote: Vihar: I've also wondered if the reason she asked me to be Farris, Knight of Flowers is because I'm special to her, or something...

introduced.name: Irminsul
introduced.how: Connected to Rukkhadevata's residual consciousness, which is contaminated and linked to the Traveler's vision
introduced.quote: Nahida: Hmm, it seems like the Traveler established a connection to Irminsul.

assumed.name: Lesser Lord Kusanali
assumed.quote: Dunyarzad: Just as promised, Traveler and Paimon! I'm so glad that you two came back to celebrate Lesser Lord Kusanali's birthday.

assumed.name: Port Ormos
assumed.quote: Dunyarzad: Speaking of which, did you manage to make your way to Port Ormos? Discover anything over there?

assumed.name: Nilou
assumed.quote: But if you ask me, I'm sure Nilou's Dance of Sabzeruz will be just as impressive!

assumed.name: Natlan
assumed.quote: Paimon: Traveler, we have to go to Natlan as soon as possible!

assumed.name: Dendro Archon
assumed.quote: Dunyarzad: Hehe... You don't have to be a vegetarian to enjoy the spread. We just use the seven foods to symbolize the seven virtues of the Dendro Archon.

assumed.name: Akasha
assumed.quote: Azar: When we return, have the Scribe draft an ordinance before the next Jnagarbha Day that prohibits public art performances. We will announce it to the public later via the Akasha.

assumed.name: Dendro Archon
assumed.quote: Aside from the Dendro Archon, the Akademiya's sages are the only ones in Sumeru who could pull off something like this.

assumed.name: Irminsul
assumed.quote: Most information in the Akasha comes from Irminsul.

assumed.name: Nilou
assumed.quote: I should escort Miss Dunyarzad to Nilou's stage.

assumed.name: Grand Sage
assumed.quote: Go celebrate the birth of that god to your heart's content.

assumed.name: Port Ormos
assumed.quote: I heard the same sound in Port Ormos.

assumed.name: Akademiya
assumed.quote: Merchant: ...Why can't we leave the city? What is the Akademiya up to now?

assumed.name: Grand Sage
assumed.quote: Guard: Don't ask me. It's not like I can tell you anything. This is a direct order from the Grand Sage.

assumed.name: Dendro Archon
assumed.quote: Paimon: Ooh, okay. Those dream-controlling creatures in the forest also get their power from the Dendro Archon, right?

assumed.name: Avidya Forest dream
assumed.quote: Traveler: Those spaces remind me of... dreams. Like the one I had in the Avidya Forest, except these have no sign of human presence.

assumed.name: Khaenri'ah disaster
assumed.quote: Nahida: As you two probably know, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata disappeared after the disaster in Khaenri'ah.

assumed.name: Akasha Terminal
assumed.quote: Paimon: What? Isn't this just an Akasha Terminal?

assumed.name: Haypasia
assumed.quote: Paimon: So in other words, the complete opposite of how Haypasia understood it...

assumed.name: Homayani family
assumed.quote: Dehya: Hey, this is my job. The Homayanis pay me, not you.

assumed.name: Dunyarzad's earlier visit
assumed.quote: Paimon: Remember how during the first Sabzeruz Festival, before the samsara started, we came here with Dunyarzad because she wanted to pick something up?

assumed.name: Nilou's Dance of Sabzeruz
assumed.quote: Paimon: Paimon still remembers when we were sitting here, and the way her eyes sparkled when she talked about Nilou's Dance of Sabzeruz...

threads.claim: The festival day seems to repeat, and the Traveler feels unexplained deja vu hinting at a loop.
threads.quote: Traveler: Why do I keep having this sense of déjà vu...?

threads.claim: The Akademiya's authority and laws are used to suppress the festival and public art.
threads.quote: Azar: When we return, have the Scribe draft an ordinance before the next Jnagarbha Day that prohibits public art performances. We will announce it to the public later via the Akasha.

threads.claim: Lesser Lord Kusanali's teachings say everything is interconnected and traced back to fate.
threads.quote: Dunyarzad: Well... According to Lesser Lord Kusanali, everything is interconnected, and all that occurs can be traced back to fate. You can say this is a pearl of old wisdom.

threads.claim: Lesser Lord Kusanali inspires people to act, giving Dunyarzad the courage to pursue her wishes.
threads.quote: Dunyarzad: To be honest, Lesser Lord Kusanali gave me the courage to do all of this. If it weren't for her encouragement, I wouldn't have taken that first step.

threads.claim: Dunyarzad's terminal illness is shown to be advancing, foreshadowing her early death.
threads.quote: Dunyarzad: The next festival... I probably won't be around by then.

threads.claim: The banned Dance of Sabzeruz leaves Nilou and Dunyarzad with an unresolved promise and regret.
threads.quote: Nilou: But you've been really looking forward to this. I don't want you to have any regrets...

threads.claim: Nahida reveals that the world is trapped in a one-day samsara that the group must escape to save Dunyarzad.
threads.quote: You, me, and everyone else are all stuck inside a one-day samsara...

threads.claim: The simple time loop explanation is rejected because it cannot account for all the phenomena.
threads.quote: A simple time loop can't explain some of the phenomena.

threads.claim: The Akasha is strongly suspected to be the cause of the loop that traps everyone.
threads.quote: The Akasha definitely has something to do with whatever's trapping us in this cycle!

threads.claim: A beep heard every night may be an Akasha operation sound that continues despite removing the terminals.
threads.quote: I feel like at the end of every day...

threads.claim: The beep is a prompt tone for Akasha operations and still sounds even after the Akasha Terminals are removed.
threads.quote: The beep is a prompt tone for Akasha operations. We still hear it every night, even though we removed our Akasha Terminals.

threads.claim: Unseen speakers discuss a phase runtime and casualties, suggesting a deliberate scheme behind the loop.
threads.quote: Phase runtime has exceeded its expected length. At this rate, there may be casualties...

threads.claim: An unseen speaker orders the harvest to continue, calling the sacrifices trivial compared to the goal.
threads.quote: Continue the harvest. Compared to what we stand to achieve, these sacrifices are trivial.

threads.claim: Dehya suspects the sages are using the Akasha to repeat the festival on purpose.
threads.quote: It wouldn't surprise me if they're using the Akasha to intentionally repeat the Sabzeruz Festival as a sick joke.

threads.claim: Dunyarzad is dying and has little time left, which motivates the group to break the samsara.
threads.quote: and... she doesn't have a lot of time left.

threads.claim: Dunyarzad's illness gets worse with each festival repetition.
threads.quote: Dunyarzad's illness has also gotten worse...

threads.claim: Nahida hides who she really is, saying knowing it will not help them find the truth.
threads.quote: Anyway, knowing who I am won't help you get closer to the truth, so you should focus on other things.

threads.claim: The divination of the Moon, illusions, and lies hints at Nahida's role, since she claims to be the Moon.
threads.quote: Hmm... I guess I'm the Moon.

threads.claim: The Traveler and Paimon feel unusually strong déjà vu, a sign they are sensitive to the loop.
threads.quote: Your sense of déjà vu is stronger than everyone else's, yes?

threads.claim: People in Sumeru are said never to dream, which the group finds strange.
threads.quote: Didn't you know that no one dreams in Sumeru? Go somewhere else if you want to find someone to daydream with, hahaha...

threads.claim: Dehya's body remembers the greatsword and her fighting skill, even though her memory is erased each day.
threads.quote: It's as if... I've already used it to fight a countless number of battles.

threads.claim: Memory erasure each night is proposed as a theory and then challenged by Dehya's evidence that she would have noticed missing money.
threads.quote: Common sense says my wallet should've emptied itself a long time ago.

threads.claim: The group has never considered leaving the city, and the Traveler suspects a clue about the loop lies there.
threads.quote: How come... we've never thought about leaving the city?

threads.claim: Nahida reveals that the group twice planned to leave the city but never returned that night, and their memories of it are gone.
threads.quote: both times, you never came back the whole night.

threads.claim: The group concludes they are not in the real world, though the reason remains unknown.
threads.quote: We're not in the real world.

threads.claim: Removing the Akasha Terminals did not stop the beep or the loop, and it puzzles Dehya.
threads.quote: We took off our Akasha Terminals... How...?

threads.claim: The strange spaces outside the city seem to be dreams, hinting that the Akasha is involved.
threads.quote: Traveler: Those spaces remind me of... dreams.

threads.claim: The Akasha is harvesting people's dreams, and Sumeru's people do not realize it.
threads.quote: Traveler: We are all in a dream. It isn't that the people of Sumeru don't dream. Rather, the Akasha is taking their dreams from them.

threads.claim: The Sabzeruz Festival may be repeating, and the team must hurry to find the truth.
threads.quote: Nahida: We don't have many more festivals to waste. Hurry and find the truth.

threads.claim: The samsara of the Sabzeruz Festival seems to end once the dream host wakes up.
threads.quote: Paimon: Have we finally escaped from the Sabzeruz samsara?

threads.claim: The Akademiya is secretly doing something big and locking down the city.
threads.quote: Merchant: ...Why can't we leave the city? What is the Akademiya up to now?

threads.claim: The sages are deliberately hiding their plans and their motives remain unknown.
threads.quote: Nahida: I think they're deliberately trying to hide something.

threads.claim: Dunyarzad's health is compromised, and the dream harvesting takes a harder toll on her.
threads.quote: Nahida: Especially those whose health is compromised to begin with... like Dunyarzad. This relentless exploitation takes an even harder toll on them.

threads.claim: Dunyarzad's fading consciousness was rescued by Nahida after the samsara broke.
