introduced.quote: Enjou: While their brothers and sisters — who 500 years before departed from their homeland — headed to the true land of wind.

introduced.name: Mare Jivari
introduced.how: a true realm that cannot be entered without Bakunawa's power
introduced.quote: Enjou: But know this, . Without the power of Bakunawa, you will never be able to enter the true Mare Jivari. Allow me to leave you a final parting gift.

introduced.name: Pyro Archons
introduced.how: former rulers whose names are carved on a stone tablet and who likely built this place to contain Bakunawa
introduced.quote: Citlali: Some of them have been eroded beyond recognition, while others are barely legible. They are the names of the former Pyro Archons.

introduced.name: Hayne
introduced.how: Enjou's alias when he posed as a tourist to befriend Papar
introduced.quote: Citlali: Papar? He's fine. Enjou told me that he previously disguised himself as a tourist and adopted the name "Hayne."

introduced.name: Exile of the Tenochtzitoc people
introduced.how: the kingdom's exiles split, with one group leaving their homeland forever and the other settling in a barren remote area
introduced.quote: Enjou: These exiles split into two different groups. One chose to accept their exile, and abandoned their homeland forever.

assumed.name: Mavuika
assumed.quote: I have to find a way to inform Mavuika, or at least leave a message that can be passed on to her...

assumed.name: Kinich
assumed.quote: Kinich even told me you've crossed paths with him before...

assumed.name: Venti
assumed.quote: Venti also mentioned something about the contamination of time in the Mare Jivari...

assumed.name: Bennett
assumed.quote: it looked like the place we went to search for Bennett before!

assumed.name: Teyvat
assumed.quote: Teyvat to Leyla, you do remember why we're here, right?

assumed.name: six heroes of Natlan
assumed.quote: Do you think this might have something to do with the story of the six heroes of Natlan?

assumed.name: The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil
assumed.quote: Do you remember that time we helped Leyla get his spirit back?

assumed.name: Monetoo
assumed.quote: They look like Monetoo, but their colors are way more vibrant, and they seem to be smarter!

assumed.name: Wayob
assumed.quote: Blast! My connection to the Wayob's been severed...

assumed.name: Archons
assumed.quote: Oh, Archons, I deserve the scolding our mothers are going to give me...

assumed.name: Gold
assumed.quote: The worst part about the beast is that it has even stronger immortality than the rest of "Gold"'s creations.

assumed.name: Tzitzimitl
assumed.quote: The Tzitzimitl can't stray too far from me, either...

assumed.name: Citlali
assumed.quote: Paimon: R—Really? Is he lying again, Citlali?

assumed.name: Granny Itztli
assumed.quote: Enjou: Don't shout so loudly, or you'll kill off all dear 's brain cells. As for your beloved Granny Itztli... She can no longer respond to you.

assumed.name: Papar
assumed.quote: Traveler: How's the employee who was acting up earlier?

assumed.name: Mavuika
assumed.quote: Citlali: I'll check with Mavuika. I have a feeling she'll know something about this place.

assumed.name: Tenoyollotzin
assumed.quote: Citlali: Now that I think about it, when Enjou was hiding inside "Tenoyollotzin," I don't think he was able to enter this place.

assumed.name: Citlalin
assumed.quote: Citlali: I let Citlalin scout the area, and it found a stone tablet behind the temple. It just so happens there were some names written on it.

assumed.name: Abyss Order
assumed.quote: Paimon: We always knew this guy wasn't like the other Abyss Order goons...

assumed.name: Mondstadt
assumed.quote: Enjou: I know how Mondstadt's old aristocracy was overthrown, how the people of Liyue began the great migration of the Guili Assembly,

assumed.name: Guili Assembly
assumed.quote: Enjou: I know how Mondstadt's old aristocracy was overthrown, how the people of Liyue began the great migration of the Guili Assembly,

assumed.name: Vindagnyr
assumed.quote: Enjou: , I have seen the glory of Vindagnyr perish, buried beneath the snow.

assumed.name: Remuria
assumed.quote: Enjou: I have touched the vessels of flesh and blood in the Moshiri Ceremonial Site, the broken colossi of Remuria,

threads.claim: The Mare Jivari mysteriously vanished about twenty years ago, and its disappearance is unexplained.
threads.quote: That is, until the whole Mare Jivari mysteriously vanished about twenty years ago.

threads.claim: No surviving records explain how the Mare Jivari disappeared, and it may be hidden by some power.
threads.quote: No extant records suggest how the Mare Jivari could have disappeared.

threads.claim: Citlali suspects the Mare Jivari was hidden by some power rather than having truly vanished.
threads.quote: If it had really disappeared, then it shouldn't be possible to perceive it in any way.

threads.claim: Asha may be Monetoo with souls, and the name may mean ashes blown from the Mare Jivari.
threads.quote: Many believe that Asha are Monetoo with a soul, and that's why they're smarter and more approachable.

threads.claim: The Asha are the key to the relic's lock and seem tied to the Mare Jivari.
threads.quote: Aha... It seems the Asha were the key we needed for the lock...

threads.claim: Bakunawa's remains may regrow into a new Bakunawa if the right conditions are met.
threads.quote: If the right conditions are met, the beast's remains could potentially still grow into a new Bakunawa once more...

threads.claim: Bakunawa was defeated through Tenoch's sacrifice and a summoned miniature Night Kingdom.
threads.quote: Through Tenoch's sacrifice. He let Sanhaj perform Phlogiston Engraving on his body in order to unleash the power of border spells.

threads.claim: A temporal disruption may have occurred in the Mare Jivari, raising questions about time.
threads.quote: Assuming the records of this ancient troupe in their heyday are accurate, it may suggest that a temporal disruption phenomenon occurred in the Mare Jivari.

threads.claim: Bakunawa's permeation may be a power that corrupts the passage of time.
threads.quote: A power that can corrupt even the passage of time...

threads.claim: The travelers may have been transported to a place that is not Natlan.
threads.quote: Maybe this isn't Natlan at all.

threads.claim: Citlali's connection to the Wayob has been severed, suggesting they are not in Natlan.
threads.quote: Blast! My connection to the Wayob's been severed...

threads.claim: The Night Kingdom's presence is sensed here, linking the place to Sanhaj's border spell.
threads.quote: This place looks like the Night Kingdom.

threads.claim: Papar has been strangely affected by something, and his erratic behavior is unexplained.
threads.quote: Lately, though, something's gotten into him.

threads.claim: The Tenoyollotzin seen earlier was actually Enjou in disguise, not Papar.
threads.quote: Wait, so the "Tenoyollotzin" we met just now was Enjou in disguise?

threads.claim: Enjou sought to sacrifice Leyla to learn about the Mare Jivari, and is pursuing its secrets.
threads.quote: Enjou just wanted to sacrifice Leyla to get information about the Mare Jivari.

threads.claim: Tenoyollotzin gathered allies from the six great tribes, tied to the six heroes of Natlan.
threads.quote: And so, Tenoyollotzin gathered allies from the six great tribes.

threads.claim: Tenoch's remains are buried at a stone structure, linking him to the six heroes' legacy.
threads.quote: To the everlasting Tenoch. His remains are buried here.

threads.claim: Leyla's carrots warn that frost will come to claim the crops, hinting at a looming threat.
threads.quote: When the field is filled with crops, frost will come to claim them.

threads.claim: The hidden palace is shrouded, and only the legacy of heroes may awaken it.
threads.quote: ...only the legacy of heroes may awaken...

threads.claim: Sanhaj cast a border spell that may have opened a passage to the Mare Jivari.
threads.quote: Sanhaj once cast a border spell.

threads.claim: A stone tablet warns of Bakunawa's revival, hinting the beast could return.
threads.quote: Stone Tablet: ...Bakunawa's revival...

threads.claim: An inscription speaks of holding back a Black Tide that must be blocked at the Mare Jivari.
threads.quote: Stone Tablet: ...before the return... must block the Mare Jivari... hold back the Black Tide...

threads.claim: Citlali suspects the Pyro Archons built this place five hundred years ago to contain Bakunawa, but their methods are unknown.
threads.quote: Citlali: I have an inkling this place may have been put together by the Pyro Archons five hundred years ago.

threads.claim: A booklet says containing the Mare Jivari is a task too big for one generation.
threads.quote: Wind-Worn Booklet: ...seal the borders, contain the Mare Jivari... not a task for just one generation...

threads.claim: A later booklet declares a task complete, hinting the containment effort finally succeeded.
threads.quote: Elegantly-Written Booklet: Task complete. Now I sing! — Isaja

threads.claim: Enjou says the true Mare Jivari can only be entered with Bakunawa's power.
threads.quote: Enjou: But know this, . Without the power of Bakunawa, you will never be able to enter the true Mare Jivari. Allow me to leave you a final parting gift.

threads.claim: Citlali's spirit trace on Enjou was consumed by a strange power, and something is wrong with the Mare Jivari.
threads.quote: Citlali: The spirit trace I left on Enjou seems to have been consumed by a strange power...

threads.claim: Enjou claims to remember many places, yet none of those memories feel like his own.
threads.quote: Enjou: But none of these places in my memory belong to me. They are like shooting stars, merely flitting across my sky with a spark, then fading away into nothing.

threads.claim: Enjou wonders whether his forgotten homeland lies within this realm of shattered time.
threads.quote: Enjou: If there truly is a homeland I have forgotten, could it be within this realm of smoldering, shattered time?

threads.claim: The Traveler suspects Enjou may be a Muratan, a question Enjou leaves unanswered.
threads.quote: Traveler: Does this mean... you're one of these Muratan people?

threads.claim: Citlali admits she could not read Enjou's intentions even at the end.
threads.quote: Citlali: That's a relief. I couldn't see what Enjou was up to... Tch, unreadable to the very end.

threads.claim: Granny Itztli reappears despite Enjou claiming he had driven her away, puzzling him.
threads.quote: Enjou: Granny Itztli...? Why, I swore I had driven you away.

threads.claim: Papar is fine after Enjou, posing as Hayne, plied him with Aphimead and he is sleeping it off.
threads.quote: Citlali: Papar? He's fine. Enjou told me that he previously disguised himself as a tourist and adopted the name "Hayne."

threads.claim: Enjou says he serves the Abyss Order but that the Order is not his home.
threads.quote: Enjou: , Paimon. I serve the Abyss Order, but the Order is not my home. What about you two? Where is your home?

threads.claim: Enjou mentions the broken colossi of Remuria, hinting at a lost past the player does not yet know.
threads.quote: Enjou: I have touched the vessels of flesh and blood in the Moshiri Ceremonial Site, the broken colossi of Remuria,

introduced.name: Ahes
introduced.how: self-introduction; a self-described Sponsian archaeologist who collects and reads wreck logs
introduced.quote: Hello, I'm Ahes. It's a pleasure to meet a new friend!

introduced.name: Sponsian
introduced.how: a white ironclad ship that sails through dreams and explores whirlpools and the abyss
introduced.quote: Ahem, the ship I mentioned is the Sponsian, a white ironclad ship that sails through dreams, and the explorer of whirlpools and the abyss...

introduced.name: Basil Elton
introduced.how: admiral whose flagship was the Sponsian; a captain who left a shipwreck and logbook behind
introduced.quote: It's the flagship of Admiral Basil Elton!

introduced.name: military conch
introduced.how: an old navy communication device used to send signals to the ship
introduced.quote: This is a military conch for communication!

introduced.name: Elynas
introduced.how: a great beast the fleet pursued and tried to stop in Fontainian waters
introduced.quote: ...Day 23 of following the great beast Elynas. We have to stop it or at least immobilize it before further damage is done to Fontainian waters...

introduced.name: Abyss monsters
introduced.how: monsters from the Abyss that the fleet fought, which legends describe
introduced.quote: They came here to fight against monsters from the Abyss...

introduced.name: Fontaine
introduced.how: a region where most ships are legally required to respond to signals
introduced.quote: Hmm, though we are in Fontaine, and most ships are required to respond to signals by law...

introduced.name: Cathuria
introduced.how: a paradise the Sponsian is said to have returned from
introduced.quote: She who's returned from the paradise of Cathuria!

assumed.name: Verenata
assumed.quote: Verenata told me! She said that you saw her in an illusion — the Sponsian, she who sails forward eternally!

assumed.name: Echoing Conch
assumed.quote: (Investigate the crate north of the Echoing Conch)

threads.claim: It is uncertain whether the transparent ship glimpsed in an illusion really was the Sponsian.
threads.quote: I'm not certain that was her, exactly, but we did see half a transparent ship...

threads.claim: Ahes insists the Sponsian is still sailing and was never truly lost.
threads.quote: I knew she wasn't gone!

threads.claim: The Sponsian is revealed to be a wreck, with only half of the ship found on the shore.
threads.quote: This wreckage must've once been the ship we were chasing earlier — or, well, half of it anyway...

threads.claim: Only the front half of the Sponsian's hull survives, and the rest of the ship is missing.
threads.quote: Well... She isn't that huge... because Captain Basil only left half of its hull behind...

threads.claim: The missing half of the ship may still be inside the sea monster that attacked it.
threads.quote: Then her other half might still be inside its body.

threads.claim: The Sponsian answers specific conch signals, like a whale responding to song.
threads.quote: She's just like a whale! You sing, and she responds.

threads.claim: Sending the correct signal makes the Sponsian appear in the distance.
threads.quote: Shh, the signal!... Wait... Her! It's her, she's over there! In the distance!

threads.claim: The Traveler hears Captain Basil's voice during a vision of the ship's last moments.
threads.quote: I heard Captain Basil's voice.

threads.claim: The fleet was chasing a great beast named Elynas before the Sponsian was destroyed.
threads.quote: ...Day 25 of following the great beast Elynas. It's been a long time since we last docked at a port, but when we got close to shore this time, only ruins welcomed us — the creature had visited this place.

threads.claim: The Sponsian was on an expedition against Abyss sea monsters when it was badly damaged.
threads.quote: 2100, visibility 6. Quiet sea, with three abyssal sea monsters emerging at four o'clock off the starboard bow.

threads.claim: The military conch is a relic from a navy that no longer exists.
threads.quote: It must be a relic left behind from when the navy still existed.

threads.claim: The Sponsian is said to have returned from a paradise called Cathuria.
threads.quote: She who's returned from the paradise of Cathuria!

introduced.name: Lepine-Pauline
introduced.how: a small-time engineer who used to supply equipment to the Fontaine Research Institute and has lost her savings
introduced.quote: I used to be an equipment supplier to the Fontaine Research Institute before that blew to pieces, and now I'm just a small-time engineer.

introduced.name: The Steambird
introduced.how: a news publication that printed the Blubberbeast story and that Lepine-Pauline read
introduced.quote: She read an article in The Steambird about a criminal who evaded Gardemek detection by disguising themselves as a Blubberbeast.

introduced.name: Gardemeks
introduced.how: sophisticated automated guardians that can identify criminals reliably
introduced.quote: In truth, Gardemeks are extremely sophisticated in their capabilities.

introduced.name: Maison Gardiennage
introduced.how: the body overseeing the Gardemeks that makes arrests and gives advice on public security
introduced.quote: They even went to the Maison Gardiennage for advice.

introduced.name: Blubberbeast incident
introduced.how: a widely reported crime story about criminals disguised as Blubberbeasts, revealed to be a fictional short story by an anonymous amateur author
introduced.quote: The Blubberbeast incident was a short story mailed to us by an anonymous amateur author, written in the style of a true story.

introduced.name: Graph Adversarial Technology
introduced.how: an image recognition research field that Lepine-Pauline invested heavily in
introduced.quote: I've invested all of my savings into Graph Adversarial Technology, and even taken out a sizeable bank loan!

introduced.name: Kamera lens prototype
introduced.how: a prototype lens for high-fidelity image capture with rapid focal length adjustment, given to the Traveler and Paimon
introduced.quote: The rapid focal length adjustment is a very useful function in its own right.

assumed.name: Mora
assumed.quote: Two hundred and seventy thousand Mora.

assumed.name: Fontaine
assumed.quote: Her aim was to improve Fontaine's public security by developing a device that could enhance Gardemeks' target-recognition capabilities...

assumed.name: Blubberbeast
assumed.quote: I read that a gang of criminals tricked the Gardemeks by disguising themselves as Blubberbeasts...

assumed.name: Opera Epiclese
assumed.quote: I'm gonna pick a fight with a Gardemek, head to the Opera Epiclese, and get a one-way ticket to the Fortress of Meropide.

assumed.name: Fortress of Meropide
assumed.quote: I'm gonna pick a fight with a Gardemek, head to the Opera Epiclese, and get a one-way ticket to the Fortress of Meropide.

threads.claim: A reported criminal disguise story may be true, and Lepine-Pauline insists it must be.
threads.quote: It's true, isn't it? It has to be!

threads.claim: The Blubberbeast incident is revealed to be a fictional short story by an anonymous amateur author.
threads.quote: The Blubberbeast incident was a short story mailed to us by an anonymous amateur author, written in the style of a true story.

threads.claim: The Fontaine Research Institute blew to pieces in a past event that ruined Lepine-Pauline's career.
threads.quote: I used to be an equipment supplier to the Fontaine Research Institute before that blew to pieces

threads.claim: Gardemeks identify criminals as reliably as the best human Gardes, so crude disguises fail.
threads.quote: They can identify criminals just as reliably as the best human Gardes, so a crude disguise isn't gonna get you far.

threads.claim: Charlotte argues that real news and news-like fiction must never be blurred, even with a good justification.
threads.quote: The boundaries between real news reports and news-like fiction must not be blurred, even when there's a compelling justification for doing so.

introduced.name: Nefer
introduced.how: Commissioner who runs a long-term partnership with the Adventurers' Guild and runs a Curatorium of Secrets
introduced.quote: More like the kind who dishes them out.

introduced.name: Curatorium of Secrets
introduced.how: Nefer's home base where she serves tea to visitors
introduced.quote: (After entering the Curatorium of Secrets)

introduced.name: Ashru
introduced.how: Nefer's cat, once fierce and now friendly
introduced.quote: Looks like Ashru's taken a real liking to you.

introduced.name: Sarin
introduced.how: Adventurers' Guild contact who handles Nefer's commissions
introduced.quote: Mr. Sarin was more than happy with my terms, so we soon came to an understanding.

introduced.name: Adventurers' Guild
introduced.how: Adventurer organization with a network that finds rare stories for Nefer
introduced.quote: The Adventurers' Guild must have quite the impressive network, tracking down a long-lost story like this...

introduced.name: long-term partnership with the Adventurers' Guild
introduced.how: Nefer pays guild adventurers for desert folk tales and sometimes returns favors
introduced.quote: They bring me stories passed down among the desert people, I pay them accordingly, and sometimes, even do them a little favor in return.

introduced.name: The Man Who Became a Mule
introduced.how: Desert folk tale, a copy of which Nefer obtained and which her father never altered at the ending
introduced.quote: Here, this is the book I asked the Adventurers' Guild to find for me. Take a look.

introduced.name: Ortba
introduced.how: Gullible fool in the tale who is kind and lends his mule to a swindler
introduced.quote: Once upon a time, in Sumeru City, there lived a fool known to all by the name of Ortba, the son of a merchant and a dancer.

introduced.name: Al-Ahmar
introduced.how: Desert power a mother petitions, which turns liars into mules in the tale
introduced.quote: To punish me, my mother went into the desert and, with her very own tears, pleaded with Al-Ahmar to teach me how to be good.

introduced.name: Sumeru
introduced.how: Region split between rainforest folk who hear wise tales and desert folk who get survival tales
introduced.quote: Tales like these, stories full of wisdom and warmth, were something only the lucky few living in the rainforests got to hear.

introduced.name: Wall of Samiel
introduced.how: Barrier that cut desert-dwellers off from civilization
introduced.quote: by the Wall of Samiel... wisdom and warmth were luxuries we couldn't afford.

introduced.name: desert folk tales
introduced.how: Desert stories whose purpose was teaching children to survive, not to be warm
introduced.quote: The stories passed down in the desert had one purpose, and one alone — to teach children how to survive.

introduced.name: village buried under desert sands
introduced.how: Nefer's village and tribe were lost to the sand in a past disaster
introduced.quote: before our little village ended up buried under the desert sands

introduced.name: Nefer's father
introduced.how: Storyteller who secretly warmed up desert tales and brought back spoils of war
introduced.quote: He used to tell me stories.

introduced.name: Nod-Krai
introduced.how: Where Nefer settled and built her life after the desert loss
introduced.quote: So, after I established myself in Nod-Krai, I started using every available channel to track down the stories my father once told me.

introduced.name: Thoth
introduced.how: The Ibis King who sent Nefer to find something that could discern truth from falsehood
introduced.quote: he was the one who sent me in search of something that could

assumed.name: Jahoda
assumed.quote: Hey, if you start taking work from Nefer, there'll be none left for Jahoda...

assumed.name: Akademiya
assumed.quote: After that, I went to the Akademiya.

assumed.name: Snezhnaya
assumed.quote: we managed to find a collector in Snezhnaya who had a copy.

assumed.name: commissions from the Adventurers' Guild
assumed.quote: Maybe I should have her give me some easy ones.

threads.claim: Thoth sent Nefer to find something that can discern truth from falsehood, and her collecting may be the key to it.
threads.quote: I figured that gathering them up might be the key to finding the answer the Ibis King was looking for.

threads.claim: Nefer's father secretly rewrote desert tales into warmer versions, and the original endings were harsher.
threads.quote: He would take these stories and change them... imbue them with more... warmth.

threads.claim: Nefer's village and tribe were buried by desert sand in a past event whose full cause is still unrevealed.
threads.quote: before our little village ended up buried under the desert sands

threads.claim: The Man Who Became a Mule is the only tale whose ending Nefer's father left unchanged, which is why she sought it.
threads.quote: This was the very last story my father ever told me — the only one whose ending he left unchanged.

threads.claim: Jahoda is away on a job Nefer assigned, and whether it was hard or where she is remains open.
threads.quote: Was that job I gave her really that difficult?

threads.claim: Nefer and Ashru arrived in Nod-Krai with no one to rely on and had to survive by being fierce.
threads.quote: That was a long time ago, when the two of us had just arrived in Nod-Krai.

threads.claim: Desert tales taught kindness but also lying and distrust, raising the question of whether deception is necessary to survive.
threads.quote: The stories taught us to be kind, but to be scarce with our trust... to lie and deceive, as long as we didn't get caught.

threads.claim: Nefer proposes a partnership with the Traveler to bring her desert stories, extending her network beyond the Guild.
threads.quote: I was just thinking... We could sign an agreement for a long-term partnership of our own.

threads.claim: Al-Ahmar is a desert power that punishes wrongdoers, such as by turning liars into mules, and it remains unexplained.
threads.quote: So, Al-Ahmar turned me into a mule to silence me and make me pay for my foul deeds through my actions instead.

introduced.name: The Chasm
introduced.how: a mine under the Millelith's protection, whose workers pray for their fallen
introduced.quote: The Chasm is under the protection of the Millelith

introduced.name: Millelith
introduced.how: soldiers who guarded the mines and fought a battle at The Chasm about 500 years ago
introduced.quote: Led by a Yaksha, the Millelith came forth to stem the tide.

introduced.name: Millelith memorial
introduced.how: an unassuming rock pile, about 500 years old, where miners pray for the fallen
introduced.quote: Well, I'm praying at this Millelith memorial.

introduced.name: Yaksha
introduced.how: the unnamed leader who led the Millelith in the ancient battle
introduced.quote: Led by a Yaksha, the Millelith came forth to stem the tide.

introduced.name: dark calamity at The Chasm
introduced.how: a calamity that swallowed The Chasm about 500 years ago, prompting Rex Lapis to order the Millelith to guard the ore veins
introduced.quote: Back then, a dark calamity swallowed The Chasm, and Rex Lapis commanded the Millelith to stand guard over the ore veins.

introduced.name: Millelith treasure
introduced.quote: It says that these stones hide another secret that might lead a discerning person to treasure that the Millelith left behind.

introduced.name: Helm of Warding
introduced.how: one of six lost items; said to defend against rockfalls and to answer only a hero
introduced.quote: The Helm of Warding, which may defend one from rockfalls...

introduced.name: Cup of Commons
introduced.how: one of six lost items, made to memorialize comradeship
introduced.quote: The Cup of Commons, made to memorialize comradeship...

introduced.name: Skyfeather
introduced.how: one of six lost items, a symbol of lofty ideals, said to come from an eagle
introduced.quote: The Skyfeather, the symbol of lofty ideals...

introduced.name: Warrior's Spear
introduced.how: one of six lost items, once used to fend off the foe
introduced.quote: The Warrior's Spear, used to fend off the foe...

introduced.name: Sundial of Ages
introduced.how: one of six lost items, used to remember the past
introduced.quote: They say that the Sundial of Ages would be remembered by all

introduced.name: The Qingce Kid
introduced.how: a self-styled hoarder who wants the treasure and calls herself or himself The Qingce Kid
introduced.quote: They call me The Qingce Kid, and no measly motley of Chasm miners is going to stop me, or I'll never show my face again out there.

introduced.name: Erge
introduced.how: a bungling treasure seeker whose note reveals the Helm was not where expected
introduced.quote: has been roughly canceled and written again twice over.

introduced.name: paralyzed Millelith soldier
introduced.how: a soldier who lost the use of his body in the battle and later became a self-taught doctor and set up the memorial
introduced.quote: One of the soldiers fell from a great height while helping to evacuate the miners and beat back the enemy, injuring his spine

introduced.name: Stone Tablet
introduced.how: a tablet inscribed by the paralyzed soldier, revealing he left Millelith armor and equipment for a future claimant
introduced.quote: (This small stone tablet has the following words inscribed on it...)

assumed.name: Rex Lapis
assumed.quote: Rex Lapis commanded the Millelith to stand guard over the ore veins.

assumed.name: Liyue
assumed.quote: With Liyue behind us, we fought bravely, warriors all — we feared death not, and not an inch did we yield.

assumed.name: Vision
assumed.quote: It is said that this memorial was something he set up to remember his comrades by after he had obtained a Vision.

assumed.name: Treasure Hoarders
assumed.quote: Those are Treasure Hoarders at the gate... Are they looking for the Millelith's treasure as well?

assumed.name: Lord of Geo
assumed.quote: Did any of those people who went into battle alongside the Lord of Geo think that they would be remembered by people across the centuries?

assumed.name: elements
assumed.quote: They have long since turned into elements and become one with the mine

threads.claim: A rumor says the memorial hides a treasure the Millelith left behind.
threads.quote: It says that these stones hide another secret that might lead a discerning person to treasure that the Millelith left behind.

threads.claim: Digging under the rock pile reveals the Millelith treasure, so the rumor was true.
threads.quote: So the Millelith treasure is real!

threads.claim: A dark calamity swallowed The Chasm five hundred years ago.
threads.quote: Back then, a dark calamity swallowed The Chasm

threads.claim: The Yaksha who led the battle is left unnamed and buried in The Chasm.
threads.quote: together with that nameless Yaksha

threads.claim: The story of the Millelith exists in many conflicting versions.
threads.quote: There are many versions of the tale, too, which sprung up over time.

threads.claim: The paralyzed soldier's later life is told as a legend that may be only partly true.
threads.quote: instead becoming a self-taught and much-famed doctor who would help those in the same situation as himself.

threads.claim: The stone tablet confirms the paralyzed soldier survived the battle and wrote his own account.
threads.quote: During the battle at The Chasm, I lost the use of my four limbs

threads.claim: The soldier wanted to die with his comrades but was stopped by Rex Lapis.
threads.quote: I attempted to join them, only to have Rex Lapis hear of it and reprimand me, waking me from my stupor.

threads.claim: The text asks how soldiers without Visions stayed loyal to a god who never favored them.
threads.quote: how did they remain loyal to a god who never showed them favor, even until death?

threads.claim: The Flower of Farsight is said to appear only to people with lofty desires.
threads.quote: the Flower of Farsight will only make itself known to those with such lofty desires

threads.claim: The Cup of Commons is said to regain its dignity someday, which is unexplained.
threads.quote: I've heard it said that the Cup of Commons will regain its dignity someday

threads.claim: The Sundial of Ages may never have been forgotten, hinting that memory outlasts time.
threads.quote: Perhaps it has never been forgotten or lost after all?

threads.claim: The memorial is presented as a lasting testament that the sacrifices will not be forgotten.
threads.quote: Just like this memorial, this place will be here a hundred, even a thousand years from now

threads.claim: Rival treasure hunters also seek the Millelith treasure and threaten the player.
threads.quote: We'll take the Millelith's treasure, thank you very much!

introduced.name: Uncle He
introduced.how: Trapped miner who craves mushroom meat and is confirmed as Uncle He
introduced.quote: Uncle He: Oooh, yes. Hee-hee, that's me-hee-hee.

introduced.name: Jinwu
introduced.how: Huishan Hall figure in charge of team safety who looks after trapped miners
introduced.quote: Khedive: You can't just kidnap me here while I was halfway through my report, Jinwu!

introduced.name: Khedive
introduced.how: Scholar from Sumeru who researches the Chasm's peculiar mushrooms
introduced.quote: Jinwu: Now that you mention it, Khedive might be able to help. After all, he's a scholar from Sumeru.

introduced.name: Qi Ding
introduced.how: Man whose daughter's toy is lost somewhere in the mine
introduced.quote: Qi Ding's been looking for his daughter's toy, but it's nowhere to be found.

introduced.name: The Chasm
introduced.how: Dangerous mine area where fungi and plants can harm ordinary people
introduced.quote: The Chasm is a dangerous place for ordinary people.

introduced.name: Huishan Hall
introduced.how: Mining organization that sets strict rules against eating Chasm fungi
introduced.quote: That's why Huishan Hall has set strict rules against eating these things.

introduced.name: Mushroom meat
introduced.how: Fungus food that is harmless to the body but impairs sanity when eaten long-term
introduced.quote: Although long-term consumption of this type of fungus — I mean, mushroom — does impair one's sanity, it doesn't hurt the body.

introduced.name: Glaze Lily
introduced.how: Flower also called Qingxin, which Tang Wuchou wants to grow in a garden
introduced.quote: How dare you call my Glaze L... I mean, Qingxin!

introduced.name: Work Handbook
introduced.how: Miner's log belonging to Uncle He that records his thoughts on the mushrooms
introduced.quote: (A miner's log, with the name "He" on its cover — probably the name of the owner.)

introduced.name: Tang Wuchou
introduced.how: Figure who claims the name and guards Glaze Lily flowers at Cinnabar Cliff
introduced.quote: Claims to be "Tang Wuchou": Yes, and the heroic Paimon! Other than the three of us, none may touch these sacred grounds!

assumed.name: Rex Lapis
assumed.quote: everyone wondered why Rex Lapis didn't protect him.

assumed.name: Floating Fungi
assumed.quote: (After defeating several Floating Fungi, more keep coming)

assumed.name: Starshroom
assumed.quote: (After picking up a Starshroom)

assumed.name: Xinyue Kiosk
assumed.quote: they're only worth a month's meals at Xinyue Kiosk.

assumed.name: Guhua training grounds
assumed.quote: He's the one who violated our Guhua training grounds!

assumed.name: Treasure Hoarder
assumed.quote: Okay, okay Uncle He, Tang Wuchou has stopped being a Treasure Hoarder already.

threads.claim: Uncle He claims mushroom meat cured his back pain and made him stronger, hinting it has real effects.
threads.quote: Ever since I started eating mushroom meat, my lower back pain left me and I got more strength.

threads.claim: Khedive explains the fungal spores entered Uncle He's ears and that the fungus impairs sanity but not the body.
threads.quote: That's because the spores of the fungi have entered his ears.

threads.claim: Khedive is curious about the long-term consequences of eating the Chasm's peculiar mushrooms and lacks a test subject.
threads.quote: Ever since I came across these peculiar mushrooms in The Chasm, I've been curious about the long-term consequences of eating them

threads.claim: The Chasm's plants and fungi may be harmful to the human body, raising questions about the place's environment.
threads.quote: Plants and fungi growing here could also be harmful to the human body.

threads.claim: Miners wonder why Rex Lapis failed to protect Uncle He when he went missing.
threads.quote: everyone wondered why Rex Lapis didn't protect him.

threads.claim: Uncle He went missing years ago and was presumed dead.
threads.quote: When he went missing a few years back, everyone wondered why Rex Lapis didn't protect him.

threads.claim: Uncle He's family held a funeral for him, though Jinwu refused to attend because no body was found.
threads.quote: To think that your family even invited me to your funeral!

threads.claim: Qi Ding's daughter's toy is lost somewhere in the mine and its recovery is left open.
threads.quote: Qi Ding's been looking for his daughter's toy, but it's nowhere to be found.

threads.claim: A figure at Cinnabar Cliff claims to be Tang Wuchou, and his true identity is left unconfirmed.
threads.quote: Claims to be "Tang Wuchou": You old thief!

introduced.name: Moon Chess
introduced.how: a tic-tac-toe-like board game played on a 3x3 night-sky grid, where the first to line up three moons wins
introduced.quote: To play Moon Chess, of course.

introduced.name: Moon Chess rotation rule
introduced.how: only three moons can be on the board, so the earliest-placed moon vanishes once the sky is full
introduced.quote: So, when the night sky is full, the moon that rose earliest will vanish.

introduced.name: Columbina
introduced.how: a moon-themed figure who can conjure a 3x3 grid by tapping the air with kuuvahki power
introduced.quote: (Columbina reaches out and taps the air with her finger, causing a 3×3 grid to appear in front of them)

introduced.name: token of promise
introduced.how: a glowing energy ball Columbina gives the Traveler as a token of their promise to play again
introduced.quote: Here, take this as a token of our promise.

assumed.name: Silvermoon Hall
assumed.quote: (Approach the large moon-shaped rock at Silvermoon Hall)

assumed.name: kuuvahki
assumed.quote: Oh, you mean the ore that glows after absorbing kuuvahki?

assumed.name: kuuhenki
assumed.quote: After that, the kuuhenki gathered some more

assumed.name: past stone-gathering trip
assumed.quote: Do you remember those stones we went out to gather last time?

assumed.name: Frostmoon Scions
assumed.quote: Ever since seeing the grids the children of the Frostmoon Scions draw on the ground

assumed.name: Nod-Krai
assumed.quote: So, it's called "Moon Chess" here in Nod-Krai, huh... Talk about giving it a local touch...

assumed.name: A Gift From Her
assumed.quote: (After A Gift From Her this mini-game is part of the weekly randomly options)

threads.claim: Columbina hints that some truth about the moons is hidden and maybe visible on her.
threads.quote: You're staring... Is the truth of the moons written on my face?

threads.claim: Paimon calls Columbina and her kind moon goddesses, hinting at a divine nature for her.
threads.quote: Hahaha... Maybe you should lower your expectations. We're not all moon goddesses...

threads.claim: Columbina describes the moons as waxing and waning in an endless cycle, linking the game to a larger cosmic rhythm.
threads.quote: Mm... The moons wax and wane in an endless cycle...

threads.claim: Columbina can wield kuuvahki to create magical effects, unlike ordinary people.
threads.quote: With a little kuuvahki, of course... You can't do that?

threads.claim: Columbina invites the Traveler back for more games and gives a token to mark their promise.
threads.quote: If you'd like... feel free to come keep me company again, sometime.

introduced.name: Columbina
introduced.how: the Trilune Goddess who now holds the power of three moons
introduced.quote: Now that you have the power of three moons, you've become more than just something that can dominate the night sky.

introduced.name: Moon Chess
introduced.how: a game played by placing moons in the night sky
introduced.quote: The Damselette: Did you forget how to place your moons in the night sky? Shall I help you?

introduced.name: The Damselette
introduced.how: the voice that comments on Columbina's moves during Moon Chess
introduced.quote: The Damselette: Perhaps... Like this?

introduced.name: Sonnet
introduced.how: goddess of the Iridescent Moon, livelier and more playful than expected
introduced.quote: The first one I saw was Sonnet, goddess of the Iridescent Moon. She was livelier than I'd imagined, more like a playful younger sister.

introduced.name: Aria of the Eternal Moon
introduced.how: the most mature of the three goddesses, a gentle natural leader
introduced.quote: Aria of the Eternal Moon, was the most mature of the three. She was a natural leader, and was most gentle to others.

introduced.name: Canon of the Frost Moon
introduced.how: a wise, far-sighted goddess who gave Columbina her moon
introduced.quote: As for Canon of the Frost Moon... she seemed both wise and far-sighted. And it was she who gave her moon to me.

introduced.name: Three Moon Goddesses division
introduced.how: the three Moon Goddesses were divided, which may have changed the world's fate
introduced.quote: that the fate of the world may have been different, had there not been division between the three Moon Goddesses.

introduced.name: Power to return home
introduced.how: the Moon Goddesses gave Columbina the power to return home
introduced.quote: That was also why they gave me the power to return "home."

assumed.name: Lauma
assumed.quote: Ah, just like Lauma, actually.

assumed.name: Teyvat
assumed.quote: Despite their differences, they loved Teyvat, and they love this home.

threads.claim: A division among the three Moon Goddesses may have altered the fate of the world.
threads.quote: that the fate of the world may have been different, had there not been division between the three Moon Goddesses.

threads.claim: The three Moon Goddesses are no longer reachable, so they cannot be thanked in person.
threads.quote: I would very much like that as well. But I fear it's no longer possible...

threads.claim: The Damselette hints that a hidden truth about the moons exists.
threads.quote: You're staring... Is the truth of the moons written on my face?

threads.claim: Columbina was empowered to return home, implying she came from somewhere else.
threads.quote: That was also why they gave me the power to return "home."

threads.claim: Canon gave her moon to Columbina, linking the goddess's power to Columbina.
threads.quote: And it was she who gave her moon to me.

threads.claim: The world continues on, and the humans the goddesses protected have survived and kept their stories alive.
threads.quote: Fortunately, this world continues onward, and the humans they protected have survived, and pass on their stories to this day.

introduced.name: Abyss
introduced.how: an enemy force that ensorcelled tribespeople and entangled Nightsouls
introduced.quote: Long ago, the tribespeople here were ensorcelled, enchanted by our enemy, and many Nightsouls became entangled by the Abyss.

introduced.name: Nightsouls
introduced.how: souls whose dream-home lies in the Night realm and who can be entangled by the Abyss
introduced.quote: The Nightsouls can find their way back to their dream-home, avoiding the blight that grips the Lord of the Night's realm.

introduced.name: Night Kingdom
introduced.how: the dream-home realm of the Nightsouls, reached through the center seal and afflicted by blight
introduced.quote: (The player is teleported to the Night Kingdom)

introduced.name: Wayob Manifestation
introduced.how: a weakened spirit manifestation of Night that the tribe relies on and that thanks the player for aid
introduced.quote: Were it not for your aid, outlander hero, we might have long been overwhelmed by our pitch-black foe...

introduced.name: seal
introduced.how: a seal that cuts the tribe off from the outside world and from the source of its faith, and must be broken
introduced.quote: This seal severs all links with the outside world, yes, but with the source of the tribe's faith also.

introduced.name: tribe ensorcelled by the Abyss
introduced.how: long ago the tribespeople were enchanted by the enemy and many Nightsouls were entangled
introduced.quote: Long ago, the tribespeople here were ensorcelled, enchanted by our enemy, and many Nightsouls became entangled by the Abyss.

assumed.name: Iktomisaur
assumed.quote: (Approach the Iktomisaur in the cave, standing on an illusory floor)

assumed.name: Wind Current
assumed.quote: (The Iktomisaur generates a Wind Current)

assumed.name: Lord of the Night
assumed.quote: the blight that grips the Lord of the Night's realm

assumed.name: Sakaw
assumed.quote: (The player is teleported back to Sakaw's location)

threads.claim: The Abyss corrupts the tribespeople and Nightsouls, and has even twisted Wayob manifestations into mimics.
threads.quote: (Defeat the mimic Abyss-corrupted Wayob Manifestation)

threads.claim: The seals cut the tribe off from the outside world and from the source of its faith, and must be broken to fight the Abyss.
threads.quote: It must be undone for there to be any fighting chance...

threads.claim: The Nightsouls' dream-home in the Night Kingdom is threatened by blight and is hard to return to.
threads.quote: The Nightsouls can find their way back to their dream-home, avoiding the blight that grips the Lord of the Night's realm.

threads.claim: The Lord of the Night's realm is gripped by a blight.
threads.quote: the blight that grips the Lord of the Night's realm

threads.claim: The fog over Tecoloapan Bay lifts once the seals are broken.
threads.quote: (The camera shows an aerial view of Tecoloapan Bay, no longer shrouded in fog)

introduced.name: Pearl Galley
introduced.how: a ship where guests board only by invitation and staff enforce that rule
introduced.quote: That was just about the most unconventional entrance any visitor has ever made to the Pearl Galley.

introduced.name: Invitation letter
introduced.how: guests must hold an invitation to stay aboard, and invited guests may invite others
introduced.quote: All the guests you see here are here by invitation. By the boss' rules, they have the right to invite other guests, too.

introduced.name: Luoxia
introduced.how: a staff member who explains the invitation rule and the Pearl Galley's visitor policy
introduced.quote: Guests are only allowed here by invitation.

introduced.name: Cui'er
introduced.how: a lowly attendant on the Pearl Galley who cannot issue invitations and has a lover ashore
introduced.quote: I'm just a lowly attendant, I don't have the right to issue invitations.

introduced.name: Chaoxi
introduced.how: a sailor on the boat who is Cui'er's lover and is currently ashore
introduced.quote: My lover's name is Chaoxi. We have made a pact, that when next we meet, he will take me away from here...

introduced.name: Sisi
introduced.how: Chaoxi's companion who is worried about his return to sea
introduced.quote: Sisi, I literally just got back from sea and right now I just need a rest.

introduced.name: Qiu'ge
introduced.how: an opera singer booked to perform on the Pearl Galley, not a guest
introduced.quote: I'm not a guest, they just booked me to come and sing here tonight.

introduced.name: Qingxin
introduced.how: a flower used to make soothing tea for a sore throat
introduced.quote: I need three Qingxin flowers to make some soothing tea, but I haven't had the chance to leave the boat.

introduced.name: Rouran
introduced.how: the boss of the Pearl Galley who personally wrote the Traveler's invitation letter
introduced.quote: His name is Rouran. You may well have met him before...

introduced.name: Pinghai
introduced.how: a ferryman stationed at the harbor who carries people between the ship and shore
introduced.quote: We have a ferryman stationed at the harbor, his name is Pinghai.

introduced.name: Liyue Harbor
introduced.how: the shore harbor where the ferry docks and Chaoxi returns to ashore
introduced.quote: Return to Liyue Harbor

introduced.name: Opera troupe
introduced.how: a performing group on the Pearl Galley whose listing can include the Traveler
introduced.quote: Right then, as discussed, I have now added your name to the list of performers in the opera troupe.

assumed.name: Aerial route
assumed.quote: You'll be pleased to know that the next time you wish to visit the Pearl Galley, you won't need to take the aerial route.

assumed.name: Captain
assumed.quote: The things I had to do to get Captain to approve my leave, honestly...

assumed.name: Opera
assumed.quote: Here for the opera, are you?

threads.claim: The boss Rouran may have had a prior connection with the Traveler that is not yet explained.
threads.quote: His name is Rouran. You may well have met him before...

threads.claim: The boss's reasons for the invitation-letter errand are left unexplained.
threads.quote: The boss must have his reasons. Far be it from me, a lowly servant, to speculate on what they might be.

threads.claim: The begging for invitation letters was a test set up by the boss, and his real invitation had already been written.
threads.quote: The whole thing about sending you around begging for an invitation letter was just a little idea our boss had.

threads.claim: Cui'er's pact with Chaoxi to leave the ship together has gone unfulfilled, leaving her waiting.
threads.quote: But I have waited and waited, and still I haven't heard anything from him.

threads.claim: Chaoxi is pressed by his crewmates to return to sea even though he wants rest and time with Sisi.
threads.quote: It's not like I want to, but perhaps this is just my lot as a sailor...

threads.claim: VIP guests refuse outsiders while regular staff and folk are willing to help them.
threads.quote: Don't you find it amusing? The VIPs are quick to turn you away without a second thought, while it's the regular folk who are happy to lend you a hand.

introduced.name: Niloofar
introduced.how: Akademiya researcher and Alrani's mentor who is searching for her
introduced.quote: I'm Niloofar, researcher at the Akademiya... You could tell, right?

introduced.name: Alrani
introduced.how: Niloofar's student who struggled with her thesis and has gone missing
introduced.quote: Alrani is my student. She's been struggling with her thesis...

introduced.name: Adventurers' Guild
introduced.how: takes commissions to search for missing people, and Niloofar hired them
introduced.quote: So I went to the Adventurers' Guild and put out a commission.

introduced.name: Akademiya
introduced.how: research institution where researchers and students write and defend papers
introduced.quote: I'm Niloofar, researcher at the Akademiya

introduced.name: Paper review process
introduced.how: Akademiya papers are reviewed on focus, references, and overlap with other papers
introduced.quote: Paper review is complicated. You have to take into account your research focus, how extensive the references are...

introduced.name: Treasure Hoarders
introduced.how: bandits who rob and steal rather than kill
introduced.quote: Sure we are, but it's not like we kill people. We just pick and steal...

introduced.name: Gobley
introduced.how: Treasure Hoarder who holds Alrani captive at the camp with his big sis
introduced.quote: Gobley: Someone's coming over here? They can't be here for the girl... right?

introduced.name: Narzam
introduced.how: Treasure Hoarder who protects Alrani for payment and introduces herself
introduced.quote: I'm Narzam. What I do... Hmph, you must've known it. I'll cut to the chase.

introduced.name: Riddle plundering
introduced.how: Narzam asks victims riddles and returns their loot if they solve them
introduced.quote: They say she would ask her victims a question when she plunders them.

introduced.name: Alrani's cage
introduced.how: Alrani burned her books at the camp and asked to be locked in a branch cage
introduced.quote: Before we got ready to make our move on her, she just plopped down beside the campfire, weeping and throwing a bunch of books into the fire...

introduced.name: Duplicate paper topic rejection
introduced.how: Alrani's paper failed review because someone else had already submitted the same topic
introduced.quote: By the time she came back with the full version of her paper, someone had submitted one with exactly the same topic, which had already passed the preliminary review!

assumed.name: Watatsumi Island
assumed.quote: The one we met at Watatsumi Island.

assumed.name: Sakoku Decree
assumed.quote: The Sakoku Decree!

assumed.name: Inazuma
assumed.quote: Alrani came back all excited from Inazuma with a paper a while ago

assumed.name: Mora
assumed.quote: She threw a bag of Mora and asked us to lock her up.

assumed.name: Elements
assumed.quote: Literature, Elements, all sorts of stuff. Even brain teasers.

threads.claim: Alrani has gone missing after her paper was rejected, leaving her whereabouts unknown.
threads.quote: She... went missing...

threads.claim: Alrani is found alive in a cage at the Treasure Hoarders' camp, resolving her disappearance.
threads.quote: Paimon: Miss Alrani, you really are here...

threads.claim: Someone else submitted a paper on Alrani's exact topic first, which raises the question of who they were.
threads.quote: By the time she came back with the full version of her paper, someone had submitted one with exactly the same topic, which had already passed the preliminary review!

threads.claim: The Sakoku Decree is hinted as the reason Alrani's paper was delayed and she fell behind.
threads.quote: The Sakoku Decree!

threads.claim: Narzam's riddle-asking plunder scheme is introduced with a riddle whose purpose is unclear.
threads.quote: Niloofar: Her question was:

threads.claim: Narzam's riddle answer was a cheeky dodge, hinting that her riddles have deeper meaning about elements.
threads.quote: My mentor answered

threads.claim: Alrani paid Narzam with money she earned from making fertilizers, a mysterious source left unexplained.
threads.quote: Don't know what's that. Don't care.

introduced.name: Byakuyakoku
introduced.how: a closed nation the speaker was born in, unknown to outsiders
introduced.quote: From your mannerisms, you are not from Byakuyakoku either.

introduced.name: Sunchildren
introduced.how: infants chosen to rule the nation, born into the role, and later interred in royal tombs
introduced.quote: After a certain number of years, an infant will be chosen as the Sunchild, gaining control over the nation.

introduced.name: Dainichi Mikoshi
introduced.how: the object the nation worships, and the source the Sunchildren were born from
introduced.quote: Here, we worship the Dainichi Mikoshi.

introduced.name: Clymene
introduced.how: a female official who attended the Sunchildren daily and asks the Traveler for help
introduced.quote: My name is Clymene. I was a female official in charge of taking care of the Sunchildren's daily lives within the Dainichi Mikoshi.

introduced.name: Sango Pearl
introduced.how: an offering the Traveler lays before the royal tombs
introduced.quote: A single Sango Pearl is all I ask, to be laid before their tombs.

introduced.name: Orupeusu
introduced.how: a Sunchild skilled in music who played the lyre
introduced.quote: Here lies Orupeusu no Mikoto, who was skilled in music as a youth, specializing in playing the lyre.

introduced.name: Surepio
introduced.how: a Sunchild who recovered from illness and learned medicine
introduced.quote: Here lies Surepio no Mikoto, who contracted a terrible illness as a young child, and upon recovering, gained some knowledge in the realm of medicine.

introduced.name: Risutaiosu
introduced.how: a Sunchild who sculpted lifelike clay figures of court officials
introduced.quote: Here lies Risutaiosu no Mikoto, who loved to imitate the craftsmen who molded with clay

introduced.name: Isumenasu
introduced.how: a Sunchild who went boating and studied a map of the country
introduced.quote: Here lies Isumenasu no Mikoto. On his free days, he would go boating, consulting his map of the country.

introduced.name: Rikoru
introduced.how: a Sunchild who built a small model of the Dainichi Mikoshi
introduced.quote: Here lies Rikoru no Mikoto. He loved to build. He once built a small-scale Dainichi Mikoshi.

introduced.name: Ion
introduced.how: a Sunchild skilled in fortune-telling who often predicted falsely
introduced.quote: Here lies Ion no Mikoto, versed in fortune-telling and sigil-signs, but who often predicted falsely, never errant only when reading the span of his own years.

introduced.name: Piramumon
introduced.how: a Sunchild who insisted there was a world beyond the skies and loved books
introduced.quote: Here lies Piramumon no Mikoto. Oft did he insist that there must be a world beyond our skies, but they were just wild claims.

introduced.name: Soul Guide's Locus
introduced.how: a sacred place with a pool where the Sunchildren's remaining souls rest, reached by opening a path
introduced.quote: This is the Soul Guide's Locus, and this is where my final thoughts remain.

introduced.name: Rite of Solar Return
introduced.how: a ceremony in which Sunchildren re-entered the Dainichi Mikoshi on their birthday
introduced.quote: Yes, and that process was known as the Rite of Solar Return.

introduced.name: Divine Bridle
introduced.how: the badge of the Sunchild's office, lost long ago, able to serve as a medium for souls
introduced.quote: If I had the Divine Bridle, perhaps, the badge of the Sunchild's office, it might just work.

introduced.name: Aberaku no Mikoto
introduced.how: an early national figure branded a traitor for trying to usurp the Sunchild's seat
introduced.quote: But it was said that he planned to usurp the seat of the Sunchild, and was branded with the crime of treason.

assumed.name: Soul Lamps
assumed.quote: Ah, the seven Soul Lamps are lit...

assumed.name: Stone shrine spirit
assumed.quote: Let's go back to the stone shrine and tell the spirit there about this.

threads.claim: The Sunchildren were manipulated puppets, yet the people hold them responsible for sins, so their innocence is disputed.
threads.quote: Innocent? Oh no, they were not.

threads.claim: Byakuyakoku may be reachable from the outside world, which the nation's people find shocking.
threads.quote: To think that there were ways to access Byakuyakoku from the outside world... Shocking news indeed.

threads.claim: Piramumon claimed a world existed beyond the skies, and was dismissed as a wild claim.
threads.quote: Here lies Piramumon no Mikoto. Oft did he insist that there must be a world beyond our skies, but they were just wild claims.

threads.claim: Aberaku's treason may be false, with hidden forces behind the record of his crime.
threads.quote: But since you say that you obtained it from his hands, perhaps there are hidden things at work that I do not understand.

threads.claim: The lost Divine Bridle is recovered and confirmed to be genuine.
threads.quote: Ahhh... This is the Divine Bridle. The genuine article indeed!

threads.claim: Memories inherited through the bridle, including those of the people, fill the gaps in the Sunchildren's souls.
threads.quote: Thus the gaps are being filled by both the Sunchildren's own memories, imprinted upon the bridle...

threads.claim: Sunchildren were believed to return to the sun's seat through the Rite of Solar Return to avoid mortal taint.
threads.quote: The Sunchildren were birthed from the Dainichi Mikoshi, and they would again return to the seat of the sun before the mortal world could taint them.

threads.claim: Byakuyakoku still hates the Sunchildren, which makes the tombs neglected.
threads.quote: This nation, Byakuyakoku, still hates those children.

introduced.name: Fanngel
introduced.how: researcher with the Fontaine Research Institute who believes a curse causes his bad luck
introduced.quote: Warriors, my name is Fanngel. I'm a researcher with the Fontaine Research Institute.

introduced.name: Fontaine Research Institute
introduced.how: research institute that saved Fanngel from the curse by teaching him to fight it
introduced.quote: In the end, it was the Fontaine Research Institute that saved me. They taught me how to fight against it.

introduced.name: Airspace Data Collector
introduced.how: big round machine that floats into the air to gather data
introduced.quote: Airspace Data Collector...? You mean that big round machine?

introduced.name: kuuvahki
introduced.how: energy source studied as a safer alternative to Arkhium, strong in thunderstorms
introduced.quote: I came here to study the safety of kuuvahki under extreme weather conditions. I believe it could be a much safer energy source than Arkhium!

introduced.name: Arkhium
introduced.how: energy source that is too dangerous to use, linked to an explosion at the Institute
introduced.quote: At its core, that accident happened because Arkhium is still too dangerous to use as an energy source.

introduced.name: Fanngel Effect
introduced.how: Fanngel's curse that makes disasters happen around him every day
introduced.quote: Things like that happen to me every — single — day. I call it the "Fanngel Effect."

introduced.name: Fonta
introduced.how: cold drink sold in vending machines, using Fanngel's cooling system
introduced.quote: In fact, that very system ended up being used in Fonta vending machines.

introduced.name: Heinry
introduced.how: leader of Fonta's development team whose team tested the drink extensively
introduced.quote: They say Heinry's team drank tens of thousands of bottles of Fonta to perfect the flavor we have today.

introduced.name: Fannta
introduced.how: proposed renamed Fonta product named after Fanngel
introduced.quote: the Institute might even rename Fonta to "Fannta" in my honor.

introduced.name: Nod-Krai
introduced.how: region with extremely dangerous weather and thunderstorms full of kuuvahki
introduced.quote: Before coming here, I learned that the extreme weather in Nod-Krai could be incredibly dangerous

introduced.name: lightning protection device
introduced.how: device installed on the collector to guard it against lightning
introduced.quote: so I made sure to install a lightning protection device on the collector, just in case.

introduced.name: assembly modules
introduced.how: parts that must be aligned with their kuuvahki side facing the collector and pushed into place
introduced.quote: So all we need to do is align the strong kuuvahki side of each assembly module with the collector, and push them into place, right?

introduced.name: Collector 2.0
introduced.how: smaller, redesigned collector that lacks lifting structure and is later given to the Traveler
introduced.quote: Why is the Collector 2.0 so much smaller than the previous one?

introduced.name: lightning rod
introduced.how: relay device that converts kuuvahki into an upward force field to draw lightning
introduced.quote: See that lightning rod over there? I set it up specially for this experiment. It can convert kuuvahki into an upward force field.

assumed.name: Raimondo
assumed.quote: Mr. Raimondo must think very highly of you.

assumed.name: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles
assumed.quote: (If Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles has been completed)

assumed.name: Abyss
assumed.quote: It sounds about as reasonable as Paimon single-handedly fighting Abyssal monsters...

assumed.name: Teyvat
assumed.quote: You'll be known around Teyvat.

assumed.name: Glider
assumed.quote: Oh, so you already have a glider!

threads.claim: Fanngel believes a curse makes abnormal weather and disasters follow him.
threads.quote: You probably won't believe me... but this abnormal weather is probably a result of my being cursed...

threads.claim: The Fanngel Effect intensifies and resists the lightning protection device and the Travelers' help.
threads.quote: The Fanngel Effect... It's intensified. Even with the lightning protection device and your help, we can't hold it back...

threads.claim: Fanngel's curse appears not to affect the Travelers or Paimon, though Fanngel himself remains under it.
threads.quote: I'm 99.5% sure that the Fanngel Effect didn't affect either of you.

threads.claim: Kuuvahki may be a far safer energy source than Arkhium.
threads.quote: I believe it could be a much safer energy source than Arkhium!

threads.claim: Initial analysis suggests kuuvahki is indeed safer than Arkhium.
threads.quote: Based on my initial analysis, kuuvahki does indeed seem safer than Arkhium.

threads.claim: The high-altitude experiment confirms kuuvahki has great potential as an energy source.
threads.quote: The experiment was a success! Just as I thought, kuuvahki has huge potential!

threads.claim: An explosion at the Fontaine Research Institute was caused by the danger of Arkhium.
threads.quote: You've probably heard about the explosion at the Fontaine Research Institute, right?

threads.claim: Raimondo envisions freeing people from their reliance on Arkhium through research on kuuvahki.
threads.quote: I hope the research results on kuuvahki will truly achieve what Mr. Raimondo envisioned — freeing people from their reliance on Arkhium.

threads.claim: Lightning strikes the collector and sends it crashing, revealing a dangerous conductive phenomenon.
threads.quote: (Lightning suddenly strikes one of the device's legs, sending it flying off into the distance)

threads.claim: The conductive phenomenon must never happen in real applications, so its cause needs to be found.
threads.quote: that conductive phenomenon we just observed must never be allowed to happen. I have to identify the cause.

threads.claim: The lightning protection device was never tested for repeated use in high kuuvahki, so its materials gave out from fatigue.
threads.quote: Because the lightning protection device inside the collector was never tested for repeated use in such a high kuuvahki environment.

threads.claim: Fanngel and the researchers value scientific progress over glory.
threads.quote: After all, what we seek has never been glory, but scientific progress itself.

introduced.name: Hilichurls
introduced.how: a menacing, very strong group that threatens the local people
introduced.quote: Whew, these hilichurls look like the mega-strong types.

threads.claim: The hilichurls may be a hunting party, raising the question of whom they hunt.
threads.quote: Paimon wonders if this is a hunting party...

introduced.name: Przheva
introduced.how: a Fatui agent who explains she is a low-ranking pawn, not an officer or frontline soldier
introduced.quote: For your information, we're neither higher-ups in power nor front-line soldiers.

introduced.name: Alexandra
introduced.how: a Fatui agent who has been caring for local children by cooking, sewing, storytelling and outings
introduced.quote: I... I cooked dinner for those kids, sewed clothes, told stories, and took them out...

introduced.name: Nika
introduced.how: a local child who keeps pestering Alexandra to take the children out to play
introduced.quote: Maybe... Maybe it was Nika? Those kids have been badgering me to take them out to play...

introduced.name: Berat
introduced.how: a local official who must report to a superior and is wary of the Fatui
introduced.quote: Ahem, anyway... Traveler, I say we go back to the city first. I'll report this to my superior and follow his order.

introduced.name: Fatui rank-and-file pawns
introduced.how: most Fatui members are low-level pawns who rarely receive any orders
introduced.quote: There are plenty of people like us, but... most of them won't get any orders all their lives.

introduced.name: Fake-death escape plan
introduced.how: Przheva and Alexandra planned to fake their deaths so they could escape the Fatui
introduced.quote: So we thought up a plan to fake death in an attempt to escape.

assumed.name: Fatui
assumed.quote: Paimon: Okay. But be careful. They are the Fatui after all!

assumed.name: Seelie
assumed.quote: Przheva: hair... and a strange Seelie. You must be the "Traveler" mentioned in the report.

assumed.name: Eremites
assumed.quote: Przheva: I happened to see a group of the Eremites heading this way on my way here.

assumed.name: Sumeru
assumed.quote: Paimon: Leaving? Do they mean... leaving Sumeru?

assumed.name: Port Ormos
assumed.quote: (Interact with the letter where Alexandra and Przheva were in Port Ormos)

threads.claim: Two Fatui agents secretly want to desert the organization and escape its control.
threads.quote: Przheva: Today is our last chance to get away from the Fatui!

threads.claim: Fatui members live under constant distrust from others, which Przheva finds unbearable.
threads.quote: Przheva: Being a Fatuus, one could only spend the rest of their life in the distrust from others.

threads.claim: Outsiders assume Fatui kindness hides ulterior motives, reinforcing the distrust.
threads.quote: Berat: Umm, but they are Fatui! Who knows if they are just acting nice but actually with ulterior motives?

threads.claim: The Fatui are involved in a secret cargo deal whose goods have been hidden away.
threads.quote: Alexandra: Yes, all hidden somewhere safe and secret.

threads.claim: A coded letter points to an old ship departing from a hidden port south of Devantaka Mountain.
threads.quote: Paimon: It says "To the south of Devantaka Mountain, the old ship leaves port."

threads.claim: A later letter says the old ship left with a half-load of cargo, though what the cargo was stays unexplained.
threads.quote: Paimon: "...The old ship left with a half-load of cargo..."

threads.claim: The planned fake death becomes real when Alexandra is injured during the monster attack.
threads.quote: Przheva: Remember our plan? Looks like now we have to do it for real.

threads.claim: The identity of whoever left the hidden box and its letters is unknown.
threads.quote: Paimon: And we don't know who left the box here.

introduced.name: Tolfin
introduced.how: Paimon's acquaintance who knows everyone and has family in Piramida
introduced.quote: Tolfin knows everyone and everything — he just might have the info we need.

introduced.name: Hiljetta
introduced.how: Tolfin's grandmother, a stern old fighter who tests challengers
introduced.quote: Tolfin: Ahem... This is my grandmother.

introduced.name: Piramida
introduced.how: town where Tolfin's family lives and where his grandmother is found
introduced.quote: I came back to visit my parents and just so happened to be running errands here in Piramida when I spotted the two of you.

introduced.name: Proofs of the Cognoscenti
introduced.how: five artifacts that must be gathered to reach the Great Treasure
introduced.quote: Hiljetta: Not bad, not bad at all! You do have promise. Here, this is the Proof of the Cognoscenti you've been seeking.

introduced.name: Great Treasure
introduced.how: the hoard that is claimed by the Treasure Hoarders' heir after the Proofs are gathered
introduced.quote: If you want to get your hands on the Great Treasure, you'll naturally need to get past me first.

introduced.name: Treasure Hoarders
introduced.how: a group now scattered across Teyvat, once a golden-age defender of Elysium that is now in decline
introduced.quote: Exactly — there are people who call themselves Treasure Hoarders in every corner of Teyvat these days. And that's where the problem lies.

introduced.name: Reed Miller
introduced.how: legendary thief who stole from the rich to help the poor and whose treasure is the Great Treasure
introduced.quote: While most of us have heard how Reed Miller stole from the rich to help the poor, very few know that the Treasure Hoarders once defended Elysium from the dark abyss...

introduced.name: Avrelian
introduced.how: another name of Reed Miller, the one who left the raven insignia
introduced.quote: I think it could only have been Avrelian who left that

introduced.name: Elysium
introduced.how: an ideal of wealth shared with the poor that the Treasure Hoarders once defended
introduced.quote: While most of us have heard how Reed Miller stole from the rich to help the poor, very few know that the Treasure Hoarders once defended Elysium from the dark abyss...

introduced.name: Royal Military Academy
introduced.how: academy where Reed Miller and classmates played at being heroic thieves
introduced.quote: It's said that back then, he liked to play the role of heroic thief with his military academy buddies, stealing from the rich and helping the poor.

introduced.name: Raven insignia
introduced.how: a keepsake derived from a noble classmate's family crest, left by Avrelian
introduced.quote: In fact, that raven insignia was derived from the family crest of his noble-born academy classmate.

introduced.name: Brahe
introduced.how: a bard and the governor's adopted son who wrote records and fabricated tales
introduced.quote: Paimon: Look, it mentions Brahe over here. Looks like he was the one who made these records.

introduced.name: Iron Coins
introduced.how: old currency whose hoard forms the treasure pile
introduced.quote: So Iron Coins were really the currency here back in the day... That means a mountain of these things could truly be called a "Great Treasure."

introduced.name: Relya
introduced.how: a flashback figure who loots a governor's treasure and vows to rewrite unjust laws
introduced.quote: Relya: Bounty Island's just up ahead. Nothing about it looks particularly special from here.

introduced.name: Silve
introduced.how: Relya's companion in the flashback raid on the treasure
introduced.quote: Silve: I hope you're right.

introduced.name: Bounty Island
introduced.how: island where the governor's marked treasure was hidden and looted in the past
introduced.quote: Relya: Bounty Island's just up ahead. Nothing about it looks particularly special from here.

assumed.name: Blue Amber Lake
assumed.quote: Have you been following us since we parted at Blue Amber Lake!?

assumed.name: Proof of the Cognoscenti at Blue Amber Lake
assumed.quote: That's what you said back at Blue Amber Lake. Sure, you helped us get the Proof of the Cognoscenti back then...

assumed.name: Adventurers' Guild
assumed.quote: We won't need to take any more commissions from the Adventurers' Guild — we can feast like kings every day!

assumed.name: Mora
assumed.quote: Paimon: Huh!? Where's all the Mora? This is just a bunch of Iron Coins!?

assumed.name: Weasel Thief
assumed.quote: Paimon: Whoa! That Weasel Thief statue is huge! And look at all those Iron Coins!

assumed.name: Explosive Barrel
assumed.quote: Paimon: What!? It dug up an explosive barrel? This is getting super dangerous!

assumed.name: Kuuvahki
assumed.quote: (Alternatively, use kuuvahki to pull down the Unipolar Crystonite on the ceiling)

assumed.name: Alia (Historical)
assumed.quote: As long as it's written in a sufficiently dashing manner, I'm sure Miss Alia wouldn't mind.

assumed.name: Snezhnograd
assumed.quote: by the time the governor notices, we'll already be in Snezhnograd.

threads.claim: The Traveler is pressed into being the Treasure Hoarders' heir, a role they did not expect.
threads.quote: Traveler: Heir to the Treasure Hoarders? Me?

threads.claim: The Traveler agrees to play the heir in a staged show, though their true motive is the treasure itself.
threads.quote: Traveler: I just want to inherit the treasure he left behind...

threads.claim: Avrelian is confirmed as Reed Miller's other name, tying the raven insignia to the legendary thief.
threads.quote: You may be more familiar with another of his names — Reed Miller.

threads.claim: The location of the Great Treasure, East of the Moon and West of the Sun, remains unknown.
threads.quote: Paimon: *sigh* Paimon still has no idea where "East of the Moon, West of the Sun" could be...

threads.claim: Tolfin hints that the treasure is beyond the horizon yet within reach, without fully explaining it.
threads.quote: Tolfin: Oh, that... Well, it's beyond the horizon, yet so close you can touch it.

threads.claim: Brahe is the governor's adopted son, and his connection to the looted treasure is left open.
threads.quote: He might be adopted, but he's still the governor's son.

threads.claim: Brahe's notes reveal he deliberately fabricated treasure-hunter tales to make people seek the Proofs.
threads.quote: All I have to do now is fabricate a few tales of treasure hunters who tried to take shortcuts but came up empty-handed

threads.claim: Entering the flashback felt like a dream and moved the Traveler and Paimon to another place and time.
threads.quote: After that, it felt like a dream, and then somehow, we ended up here...

threads.claim: Relya dreams of raising an Elysium for her people on the land that once belonged to them.
threads.quote: One day, I'll raise an Elysium that belongs to us on this land — a land that has always belonged to us!

threads.claim: Tolfin's grandmother still longs to restore the Treasure Hoarders' glory from Reed Miller's era.
threads.quote: While we might be able to face reality, my stubborn old grandmother still dreams of a day when the Treasure Hoarders can restore their glory from the days of Reed Miller.

threads.claim: Reed Miller's note urges the finder to hide the treasure quietly and let the legend of the Proofs keep circulating.
threads.quote: Please take these treasures, which belong to you alone, away quietly.

threads.claim: Tolfin has been withholding information about the trial and the Treasure Hoarders, and his reasons are unclear.
threads.quote: Traveler: Then why didn't you tell us about it back at Blue Amber Lake...?

threads.claim: The Treasure Hoarders' golden age is described as the best and worst of times, a past that cannot return.
threads.quote: It was the Treasure Hoarders' golden age — it was the worst of times, and yet somehow it was also the best.

threads.claim: The earth remembers events that human oral history may lose, hinting that the past is still recoverable.
threads.quote: It seems the earth remembers far more than we could ever imagine — as a storyteller, I can't help but feel humbled by that...

introduced.name: Harrison
introduced.how: a merchant who runs a hidden camp on Ritou to move goods
introduced.quote: Harrison: I'm, ah, moving goods! Moving goods...

introduced.name: Ritou
introduced.how: an island where doing business is hard
introduced.quote: Harrison: I mean, you know that doing business is hard here on Ritou. This camp is... well, you can consider it a little trick of mine.

introduced.name: Harrison's hidden camp
introduced.how: a camp behind a passageway, set up as a trick to move goods
introduced.quote: Paimon: That camp actually has a passageway here. So weird...

introduced.name: Dawn Winery
introduced.how: a winery that sent a test batch of new product to Ritou
introduced.quote: Harrison: He then got a test batch of new product from the Dawn Winery, which was just shipped here.

introduced.name: Narukami Island
introduced.how: reachable from Ritou by a small boat that lets you sneak over
introduced.quote: Harrison: Using that boat, you can sneak over to Narukami Island from here. Convenient, huh?

introduced.name: Electro Slimes
introduced.how: slimes that came jumping out of a loosened bottle cap and attacked
introduced.quote: Harrison: But I never expected that a whole bunch of slimes would come jumping out of the unscrewed cap. What a strange occurrence.

introduced.name: alcohol-making ingredients
introduced.how: brewing ingredients shipped in boxes, one bottle with a loose cap
introduced.quote: Harrison: Some days back, I commissioned a... friend to ship me some alcohol-making ingredients from Mondstadt.

assumed.name: slimes
assumed.quote: Paimon: Oh wait, that's Harrison! Looks like he's been surrounded by slimes...

threads.claim: Harrison's hidden camp and sneaking boat suggest he is moving goods while avoiding notice.
threads.quote: Harrison: Using that boat, you can sneak over to Narukami Island from here. Convenient, huh?

threads.claim: Slimes emerged from a bottle cap and went berserk, and the cause is left unexplained.
threads.quote: Harrison: Argh! What's... what's with these slimes! It's like they've gone berserk!
